B12C001.summary: After the war the Pandavas spend a month mourning on the banks of the Bhagirathi, and sages come to console Yudhishthira. Narada praises his victory, but Yudhishthira says it feels like a defeat and reveals that Karna, whom Arjuna killed, was Kunti's secret firstborn and the Pandavas' elder brother. He asks Narada to explain Karna's past, which begins the story of Karna's curse.

scenes.B12C001S01: The Pandavas mourn after the war, sages console Yudhishthira, and he confesses that Karna, killed by Arjuna, was his secret elder brother.

shots.B12C001S01H01: Heading: the Rajadharmanusasana Parva section begins.
shots.B12C001S01H02: Opening invocation to Narayana, Nara and Saraswati.
shots.B12C001S01H03: Vaisampayana describes the month of mourning on the Ganga's banks, the sages who visit Yudhishthira, and Narada's praise of the victory with his question about whether the king is still grieving.
shots.B12C001S01H04: Yudhishthira replies that the victory feels like a defeat because of the kinsmen killed, then reveals that Karna was Kunti's hidden son and asks Narada to tell his story.

B12C002.summary: Narada tells the story of Karna's training and curse. Envious of Arjuna, Karna asks Drona for the Brahma weapon and is refused, so he goes to Rama and claims to be a Brahmin of Bhrigu's race. After he accidentally kills a Brahmin's sacred cow, the Brahmin curses him that his chariot wheel will sink into the earth and his foe will take his head in battle. This curse explains how Karna's death was foretold.

scenes.B12C002S01: Narada explains how Karna trained under Drona and Rama, and how he came to be cursed for killing a sacred cow.

shots.B12C002S01H01: Vaisampayana says Narada, having been asked, begins to tell how Karna came to be cursed.
shots.B12C002S01H02: Karna, envious of Arjuna, is refused the Brahma weapon by Drona, learns it from Rama under a false Brahmin claim, and is cursed after accidentally killing a sacred cow.

B12C003.summary: While Karna is learning from Rama, a worm bites his thigh as Rama sleeps on his lap, and Karna endures the pain silently so as not to wake his teacher. When Rama finds out, he learns that Karna is a Suta and not a Brahmin, and he curses that the Brahma weapon will fail Karna in battle against an equal. The episode shows Karna's patience and also the deceit that brought his downfall.

scenes.B12C003S01: Rama teaches Karna the Brahma weapon, a worm attacks Karna, and Rama curses him for deceiving him about his birth.

shots.B12C003S01H01: Narada tells how Karna endures a worm's bite so as not to wake Rama, and how Rama, learning he is a Suta, curses the Brahma weapon to fail him against an equal.

B12C004.summary: Karna, now with Duryodhana, goes to a bride-choosing in the city of Rajapura, where many kings hope to win the princess. Duryodhana seizes the maiden and drives away, and Karna beats back the kings who chase them. The episode shows Karna's martial skill and his loyalty to Duryodhana.

scenes.B12C004S01: Duryodhana carries off a princess at a bride-choosing in Rajapura, and Karna defeats the kings who pursue them.

shots.B12C004S01H01: Narada says Duryodhana carries off the maiden from the bride-choosing at Rajapura, and Karna drives back the kings who give chase.

B12C005.summary: Jarasandha, king of Magadha, challenges Karna after hearing of his fame, and Karna nearly overpowers him. Jarasandha concedes and gives Karna the town of Malini, so Karna comes to rule Champa as well as Anga. Narada then lists the curses, boons and schemes that led to Karna's death and tells Yudhishthira not to grieve for him.

scenes.B12C005S01: Karna defeats Jarasandha and is given Malini, and Narada lists the causes of Karna's death and urges Yudhishthira not to grieve.

shots.B12C005S01H01: Narada describes Karna's fight with Jarasandha, his rise to rule Champa, and the curses and schemes behind his death, then urges Yudhishthira not to grieve.

B12C006.summary: Narada falls silent, and Yudhishthira sinks into sorrow. Kunti, herself distressed, tells him that she and Surya tried to persuade Karna to join his brothers, but he refused. Yudhishthira blames her for keeping the secret, curses all women never to keep a secret, and falls into despair over his lost kin.

scenes.B12C006S01: Narada falls silent, Kunti explains her failed attempts to reconcile Karna, and Yudhishthira blames her and despairs.

shots.B12C006S01H01: Narada falls silent and Yudhishthira grieves; Kunti says she and Surya failed to win Karna over, and Yudhishthira blames her and curses women to keep no secrets.

B12C007.summary: Yudhishthira mourns Karna and the other dead, blaming the war on Duryodhana, Dhritarashtra and his own covetousness. He calls the battle a kind of self-slaughter and finds no pleasure in the kingdom he has won. He resolves to give up the throne, go to the forest, and asks Arjuna's leave, which sets up Arjuna's reply.

scenes.B12C007S01: Yudhishthira mourns the dead, blames Duryodhana and Dhritarashtra, and resolves to give up the kingdom for the forest.

shots.B12C007S01H01: Yudhishthira grieves for Karna and the slain kinsmen, blames the war on Duryodhana, and announces he will renounce the kingdom and go to the woods.

B12C008.summary: Arjuna rebukes Yudhishthira for wanting to give up the kingdom, calling it a weak and foolish choice and arguing that a king who lives by begging cannot win fame. He argues that wealth is the basis of all virtue, pointing to Nahusha and to the gods, who gained their place through strife. He urges Yudhishthira to rule and to perform a great sacrifice, making the case for kingly action over renunciation.

scenes.B12C008S01: Arjuna argues that wealth and kingly duty require Yudhishthira to rule and perform sacrifices rather than renounce.

shots.B12C008S01H01: Arjuna rebukes Yudhishthira's plan to renounce, argues that wealth is essential to virtue and that kings must hold and rule, and urges him to perform a great sacrifice.

B12C009.summary: Yudhishthira replies that he will go to the forest whatever Arjuna advises. He describes in detail the austere life he intends to lead: begging for food, avoiding injury to any creature, and remaining detached from pleasure and pain. He calls worldly life a fleeting illusion bound by birth and death, and says he wants a permanent, eternal state.

scenes.B12C009S01: Yudhishthira rejects Arjuna's advice and describes at length the forest renunciation he intends to undertake.

shots.B12C009S01H01: Yudhishthira tells Arjuna he will live as a forest ascetic, begging for food, avoiding all injury, and detached from worldly life, which he sees as an illusion bound by death.

B12C010.summary: Bhimasena rebukes Yudhishthira, saying his judgment has been clouded by too much scripture and that giving up the kingdom after such a war would make the slaughter pointless. He argues that Kshatriyas must act, that renunciation is not a fit path for a warrior king, and that forest life alone does not win heaven. The chapter sets out the opposing view from another of the Pandava brothers.

scenes.B12C010S01: Bhimasena rebukes Yudhishthira's plan to renounce, arguing that Kshatriyas must act and cannot earn heaven through forest life alone.

shots.B12C010S01H01: Bhimasena says Yudhishthira's understanding has gone astray, that renunciation is improper for a Kshatriya, and that one must act to gain success.

B12C011.summary: Arjuna tells an old story in which Sakra (Indra), in the form of a golden bird, rebukes young Brahmin ascetics who gave up home for the forest. The bird teaches that the Vedic rites, sacrifice and the householder's duties are the true path to heaven. The ascetics return to domestic life, and Arjuna urges Yudhishthira to follow their example and rule the earth.

scenes.B12C011S01: Indra as a golden bird rebukes young ascetics who abandoned home, and teaches the value of sacrifice and the householder's duties.
scenes.B12C011S02: The ascetics give up renunciation for household life, and Arjuna urges Yudhishthira to rule.

shots.B12C011S01H01: Arjuna begins an old story: Indra, as a golden bird, rebukes young Brahmin ascetics who left home for the forest and says they are not true eaters of sacrificial remnants.
shots.B12C011S01H02: The ascetics ask the bird what is good for them, saying his words inspire faith.
shots.B12C011S01H03: The bird says he will speak true and useful words if they do not turn against their better selves.
shots.B12C011S01H04: The ascetics agree to listen and ask him to instruct them.
shots.B12C011S01H05: The bird teaches that cows, gold, mantras and Brahmins are the highest of their kinds, that Vedic rites lead to success, and that the householder's life is the field of success.
shots.B12C011S02H01: Arjuna concludes that the ascetics gave up renunciation for household life, and urges Yudhishthira to rule the wide earth with that wisdom.

B12C012.summary: Nakula, the twin, answers Arjuna with a long argument that action and the householder's life are the proper path. He says the gods, ancestors and learned Brahmins all depend on sacrifice and duty, that true renunciation is inner detachment, and that a king who keeps the wealth won in war without sacrificing shows a lack of faith. He also warns that a king who neglects his subjects becomes an embodiment of Kali, the age of decline, and urges Yudhishthira not to grieve.

scenes.B12C012S01: Nakula argues that householder life, sacrifice and duty are superior to renunciation, and urges Yudhishthira to govern and give gifts.

shots.B12C012S01H01: Vaisampayana says Nakula, having heard Arjuna, speaks to Yudhishthira with reasoned argument, aiming to change his brother's mind.
shots.B12C012S01H02: Nakula says the gods depend on action, the Pitris sustain life through action, and the learned who follow the Vedas reach the highest heaven.
shots.B12C012S01H03: Nakula argues that householder life is superior, that true renunciation means inner detachment, and that a false renouncer stays bound by desire; he warns that a king who fails to protect and give is an embodiment of Kali, and tells Yudhishthira not to grieve.

B12C013.summary: Sahadeva argues that giving up outward things brings no success while inner desire remains. He says the soul is eternal, so killing a body is not real slaughter, and that a king who holds the earth but does not enjoy it wastes his life. He also says a hermit still attached to the world lives in Death's jaws, and asks Yudhishthira to forgive his blunt words.

scenes.B12C013S01: Sahadeva argues that inner detachment matters more than outward renunciation, that the soul is eternal, and that a king should enjoy the earth he holds.

shots.B12C013S01H01: Sahadeva says giving up outward things is not enough without inner detachment, that the soul's eternity bears on the question of killing, and that a king must enjoy his earth; he then asks pardon for his words.

B12C014.summary: Draupadi, silent until now, speaks to Yudhishthira while his brothers sit around him. She reminds him of his earlier vow to defeat Duryodhana and enjoy the earth, argues that a king must use the rod of punishment, and says his retreat is a kind of madness that will spread to his brothers. She lists his conquests and urges him to rule, sacrifice and give gifts to Brahmins.

scenes.B12C014S01: Draupadi rebukes Yudhishthira, reminds him of his vow to fight Duryodhana, lists his conquests, and urges him to rule and sacrifice.

shots.B12C014S01H01: Vaisampayana says Draupadi, seated among the brothers, turns to Yudhishthira, who has stayed silent after his brothers' speeches.
shots.B12C014S01H02: Draupadi reproaches Yudhishthira for his retreat, reminds him of his vow to slay Duryodhana, argues that a king must use force, lists the continents he has conquered, and urges him to rule and perform sacrifices and gifts.

B12C015.summary: Arjuna argues that the rod of chastisement, meaning force and punishment, is what upholds righteousness, wealth and order, and that without it the strong would devour the weak. He says all creatures live by harming one another, that the gods themselves are slayers, and that killing an armed enemy in a just fight brings no sin, since the soul cannot be slain. He urges Yudhishthira to take up the rod, rule the kingdom and perform sacrifices.

scenes.B12C015S01: Arjuna argues that punishment and force sustain dharma and order, that killing is part of life, and that Yudhishthira must rule.

shots.B12C015S01H01: Vaisampayana says Arjuna speaks again after Draupadi's words, showing proper respect for his eldest brother.
shots.B12C015S01H02: Arjuna argues that the rod of chastisement is the basis of righteousness, that creatures live by devouring one another, that the gods are slayers too, and that Yudhishthira should take up the rod, rule and sacrifice.

B12C016.summary: Bhima, holding back his anger, rebukes Yudhishthira for his inaction and his clouded judgment. He compares grief to a sickness of body and mind and says Yudhishthira is dwelling on past woes, recalling the family's humiliations and hardships such as Draupadi's disgrace and the exile. He argues that the real battle now is with his own mind, urges a horse-sacrifice, and says Duryodhana has been slain.

scenes.B12C016S01: Bhima accuses Yudhishthira of being clouded by grief, recalls the family's past humiliations, and urges him to rule and hold the horse-sacrifice.

shots.B12C016S01H01: Bhima says Yudhishthira's mind is clouded by grief, compares mental and bodily illness, recalls past humiliations, calls the present struggle one with his own mind, and urges a horse-sacrifice.

B12C017.summary: Yudhishthira answers Bhima that desire can never be fully satisfied, and that a king with one stomach gains nothing from endless craving for power. He praises renunciation and inner calm, citing King Janaka's verse about having nothing even when his city burns. He ends by saying that understanding, not outward forms, is the supreme good.

scenes.B12C017S01: Yudhishthira replies to Bhima that desire is endless, praises renunciation and detachment, and says understanding is what matters most.

shots.B12C017S01H01: Yudhishthira answers that desire cannot be filled, urges Bhima to conquer his appetite, praises renunciation, quotes Janaka's verse, and concludes that understanding is supreme.

B12C018.summary: Arjuna retells the tale of King Janaka of Videha, who gave up his kingdom to live as a beggar. His queen rebukes him that he has abandoned his duties to gods, guests and ancestors, and that a giver who sustains others is more honoured than a beggar. Arjuna then concludes that householders who practise charity, truth and worship can reach the regions of bliss.

scenes.B12C018S01: Arjuna tells the story of Janaka and his queen, whose rebuke favours householders over empty renunciation, and then concludes that householders can reach bliss.

shots.B12C018S01H01: Arjuna tells the tale of King Janaka, who gave up his kingdom to beg, and of his queen's sharp rebuke that a giver of food is more honoured than a beggar.
shots.B12C018S01H02: Arjuna concludes that householders who practise charity, truth and worship can reach the regions of bliss.

B12C019.summary: Yudhishthira answers Arjuna respectfully but firmly, saying Arjuna knows war but not the deeper scriptures. He ranks renunciation and knowledge of Brahma above penance, and denies that wealth is the highest good. He describes the northern path of renunciation and the southern path of action, and concludes that men reach Brahma through asceticism, intelligence and renunciation.

scenes.B12C019S01: Yudhishthira rebukes Arjuna's view of wealth and argues that renunciation and knowledge of Brahma lead to the highest good.

shots.B12C019S01H01: Yudhishthira says Arjuna knows war but not the scriptures, ranks renunciation and knowledge of Brahma above wealth, describes the northern and southern paths, and concludes that Brahma is reached by asceticism and renunciation.

B12C020.summary: The ascetic Devasthana answers Yudhishthira by arguing that a king who has won the earth should not abandon it, and that wealth belongs to sacrifice. He says the Creator made wealth for sacrifice and man to tend it, and he cites Indra, Mahadeva, Marutta and Harischandra as examples of great sacrifices that won glory. He concludes that everything should be devoted to sacrifice.

scenes.B12C020S01: Devasthana argues that wealth belongs to sacrifice and that a king who has won the earth should not abandon it.

shots.B12C020S01H01: Vaisampayana says that after Yudhishthira stops, the eloquent ascetic Devasthana speaks to the king.
shots.B12C020S01H02: Devasthana argues that a king should perform great sacrifices rather than renounce, that wealth is made for sacrifice, and that Indra, Mahadeva, Marutta and Harischandra won glory through it.

B12C021.summary: Devasthana continues with a teaching that Vrihaspati gave to Indra, in which contentment is called the highest bliss. Vrihaspati says people follow many different paths, and that the best religion is non-injury, truthfulness and compassion. He describes a righteous king who hands his crown to his son and retires to the forest, and says such a king wins good fruit in this world and the next.

scenes.B12C021S01: Devasthana quotes Vrihaspati's teaching that contentment and non-injury are the highest religion, and that a righteous king who retires to the forest is rewarded.

shots.B12C021S01H01: Devasthana quotes Vrihaspati's teaching to Indra: contentment is the highest bliss, non-injury is the best religion, and a righteous king who passes on his crown and retires to the forest wins good fruit.

B12C022.summary: Arjuna again urges Yudhishthira to act, saying that death in battle is the proper end for a Kshatriya, while renunciation and penance belong to Brahmins. He tells Yudhishthira to perform sacrifices and charity, as Indra did while fighting as a warrior. He says the slain have gained the highest end and that destiny cannot be resisted.

scenes.B12C022S01: Arjuna urges Yudhishthira to act as a Kshatriya, perform sacrifices, and accept that the dead have gained the highest end.

shots.B12C022S01H01: Arjuna argues that death in battle is a Kshatriya's proper end, that Yudhishthira should act and perform sacrifices as Indra did, and that the dead have gone to the highest end and fate cannot be resisted.

B12C023.summary: Yudhishthira stays silent, and Vyasa backs Arjuna: the householder's life is the highest duty, and a king's duties include wielding the rod of punishment. Vyasa tells of the brothers Sankha and Likhita, in which Likhita takes fruit without asking and confesses to King Sudyumna, who cuts off his hands as punishment. Sankha says the punishment has purified Likhita, whose hands return through penance, and Vyasa concludes that ruling by punishment is a king's proper duty.

scenes.B12C023S01: Vyasa backs Arjuna, praises householder life and the rod of punishment, and tells the tale of Likhita and Sankha.
scenes.B12C023S02: Vyasa concludes that ruling and punishing are a king's duty, and that shaving the head is not.

shots.B12C023S01H01: Vaisampayana says Yudhishthira remains silent after Arjuna's speech, and Vyasa, the island-born sage, speaks.
shots.B12C023S01H02: Vyasa says Arjuna is right: householder life is the highest duty, a king must support others, and wielding the rod of punishment is the chief Kshatriya duty.
shots.B12C023S01H03: Yudhishthira asks how King Sudyumna gained his highest success.
shots.B12C023S01H04: Vyasa tells how Likhita, eating fruit from his brother Sankha's hermitage without asking, goes to King Sudyumna and asks for punishment.
shots.B12C023S01H05: Vyasa continues: Sudyumna cuts off Likhita's hands, Sankha says the punishment has purified him, and Likhita's hands return through his penances.
shots.B12C023S02H01: Vyasa concludes that Sudyumna gained eminence by ruling, that punishing wrongdoers is the king's duty, and that shaving the head is not.

B12C024.summary: Vyasa urges Yudhishthira to enjoy the kingdom with his brothers, pay his debts to gods, ancestors and guests, and perform great sacrifices before he ever takes up the later stages of life. He lays out a king's duties: protect subjects impartially, punish robbers, and rely on learned counsel. He illustrates these duties with King Hayagriva, who died in battle after ruling righteously and is now in heaven, and whose battle is described as a sacrifice.

scenes.B12C024S01: Vyasa urges Yudhishthira to rule, sacrifice and protect his subjects, and tells the story of King Hayagriva.

shots.B12C024S01H01: Vyasa urges Yudhishthira to enjoy his kingdom and sacrifice, lays out a king's duty to protect subjects and punish robbers, and tells how Hayagriva, slain in battle after righteous rule, now enjoys heaven.

B12C025.summary: Yudhishthira says his kingdom brings him no joy, and the lamentations of the widowed women keep him from peace. Vyasa replies that Time governs all events, that no one truly slays or is slain, and that grief grows when indulged. He teaches that happiness and sorrow alternate and should be borne with an untroubled mind, and that a king's sacrifice is battle while his yoga is good government.

scenes.B12C025S01: Yudhishthira laments his grief, and Vyasa answers that Time governs all, grief should be borne calmly, and a king's sacrifice is battle and governance.

shots.B12C025S01H01: Vaisampayana says Yudhishthira, seeing Arjuna angry, bows to Vyasa and prepares to answer.
shots.B12C025S01H02: Yudhishthira says the kingdom gives him no joy, and that the cries of widows and mothers keep him from peace.
shots.B12C025S01H03: Vaisampayana says Vyasa, skilled in yoga and the Vedas, now speaks to Yudhishthira.
shots.B12C025S01H04: Vyasa says Time governs all events, no one truly slays or is slain, grief grows when indulged, happiness and sorrow alternate, and a king's sacrifice is battle while his yoga is good government.

B12C026.summary: Yudhishthira replies to Arjuna that wealth is not the only path, since sages gain heaven through study, penance and contentment. He notes the southern path of action and the northern path of yoga, and warns that wealth brings injury to others, anxiety and sin. He argues that wealth belongs to sacrifice and should go to deserving people, not be squandered on desire or given to the unworthy.

scenes.B12C026S01: Yudhishthira argues that sages gain heaven without wealth, that wealth brings sin, and that it should be spent on sacrifice and worthy gifts.

shots.B12C026S01H01: Yudhishthira argues to Arjuna that the poor can reach heaven, that sages gain bliss through study and contentment, that wealth brings injury and sin, and that it must go to sacrifice and worthy recipients.

B12C027.summary: Yudhishthira grieves for the fallen heroes, including Bhishma, Drona, Abhimanyu, Karna and his own sons, and blames himself for their deaths. He confesses his deceit toward Drona about Ashvatthama, and declares that he will fast to death. Vyasa stops him, saying that all is destiny and that work and skill, not idleness, bring success.

scenes.B12C027S01: Yudhishthira laments the deaths of his kin and teachers and resolves to fast to death; Vyasa counsels that all is destiny and that one must act.

shots.B12C027S01H01: Yudhishthira laments the fallen heroes, confesses his guilt over Bhishma, Drona and Karna, and resolves to fast to death.
shots.B12C027S01H02: Vaisampayana says Vyasa restrains Yudhishthira and tells him this cannot be.
shots.B12C027S01H03: Vyasa says all this is destiny, that union ends in dissolution, and that work and skill, not idleness, bring success, so Yudhishthira must act.

B12C028.summary: Vyasa tells Yudhishthira the story of Asma's discourse. King Janaka of Videha asks the Brahmin Asma how to act when kin and wealth are gained or lost, and Asma explains that joy and grief come through destiny, that prosperity breeds vanity, and that death and decay cannot be escaped. He describes family ties as the passing company of travellers at an inn and urges study, sacrifice and righteous rule, which frees Janaka from grief. Vyasa closes by urging Yudhishthira to cast off his grief and enjoy the earth he has won.

scenes.B12C028S01: Vyasa tells the tale of Asma's answer to Janaka on grief and impermanence, and urges Yudhishthira to cast off his grief and rule.

shots.B12C028S01H01: Vaisampayana says Vyasa eases the grief of Yudhishthira, who had resolved to end his own life.
shots.B12C028S01H02: Vyasa introduces the old story of Asma's discourse, in which King Janaka of Videha seeks counsel in his sorrow.
shots.B12C028S01H03: Janaka asks how a man should behave when kinsmen and wealth are gained or lost.
shots.B12C028S01H04: Asma replies that joy and grief come by destiny, that death is unavoidable, and that kin are like travellers at an inn, so one should study, sacrifice and rule righteously; Vyasa then urges Yudhishthira to cast off grief and enjoy the earth.

B12C029.summary: Arjuna asks Krishna to comfort the silent Yudhishthira. Krishna (Vasudeva) says the fallen heroes died bravely and are beyond recall, and then recounts Narada's counsel to King Srinjaya, who grieved for his dead son. Narada lists many great kings, such as Marutta, Bharata, Rama and Yayati, who all died despite their sacrifices and gifts, and so Srinjaya should not grieve; Narada then restores Srinjaya's son to life.

scenes.B12C029S01: Krishna tells Yudhishthira not to grieve for the heroes who died in battle, and Narada tells Srinjaya that great kings died too, so he should not grieve for his son.
scenes.B12C029S02: Srinjaya is freed from grief, and Narada promises to return his dead son, Suvarnashthivin, to life.

shots.B12C029S01H01: Vaisampayana says Yudhishthira remains silent, and Arjuna turns to Krishna.
shots.B12C029S01H02: Arjuna asks Madhava to comfort Yudhishthira, since the family has again fallen into great danger.
shots.B12C029S01H03: Vaisampayana says Krishna turns to Yudhishthira, takes his hand, and begins to speak.
shots.B12C029S01H04: Krishna tells Yudhishthira the fallen heroes are beyond recall and have won heaven, then recounts Narada's counsel to Srinjaya, listing ancient kings who died despite their great sacrifices and gifts.
shots.B12C029S01H05: Srinjaya says Narada's discourse has freed him from grief and asks Narada to restore his son through his grace.
shots.B12C029S02H01: Narada begins by promising to give Srinjaya back his son.
shots.B12C029S02H02: Narada names the son as Suvarnashthivin, given by Parvata and now dead.
shots.B12C029S02H03: Narada says the boy, golden in splendour, will live a thousand years.

B12C030.summary: Yudhishthira asks how Srinjaya's son came to be called Suvarnashthivin and why he died in childhood. Krishna relates that the sages Narada and his nephew Parvata, guests of Srinjaya, cursed each other after Narada fell in love with the king's daughter Sukumari. Narada was cursed to appear as an ape, and the two later lifted their curses. Krishna says Narada himself is present and can explain the rest.

scenes.B12C030S01: Krishna recounts how Narada and Parvata quarrelled over Narada's love for Sukumari, cursed each other, and later lifted the curses.

shots.B12C030S01H01: Yudhishthira asks how Srinjaya's son came to be called Suvarnashthivin, why Parvata gave him, and why he died so young.
shots.B12C030S01H02: Krishna tells how the sages Narada and Parvata, guests of Srinjaya, quarrelled over Narada's love for the king's daughter, cursed each other, and later freed each other from the curses.
shots.B12C030S01H03: Vasudeva says Narada was himself involved and is present, and will tell Yudhishthira everything.

B12C031.summary: Narada tells Yudhishthira the rest of the story. Srinjaya asks Parvata for a long-lived, heroic son, and Parvata grants a son named Suvarnashthivin but warns that he will not live long. Indra, fearing the boy, sends a thunderbolt in the form of a tiger that kills the five-year-old prince by the Bhagirathi. Narada restores the boy to life with Indra's permission, and the prince later rules for a very long time.

scenes.B12C031S01: Narada explains that the boy was killed by a tiger sent by Indra, that he restored him to life, and that the prince later ruled a long reign.

shots.B12C031S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Narada to tell of the child said to have produced gold waste, and Narada begins his account.
shots.B12C031S01H02: Narada tells how Srinjaya received a boon of a son, how Indra sent a tiger to kill him, how Narada restored him, and how the prince later ruled, closing with advice that Yudhishthira rise and perform great sacrifices.

B12C032.summary: Vyasa tells Yudhishthira that protecting subjects and punishing wrongdoers is a king's duty, and that the Kauravas were transgressors who had to be stopped. Yudhishthira confesses that the deaths he caused for the kingdom still burn in him. Vyasa asks whether man or the Supreme Being acts, argues with the example of an axe that the one who cuts is responsible, and urges Yudhishthira to live and perform expiations rather than give up his life.

scenes.B12C032S01: Vyasa tells Yudhishthira that kings must punish wrongdoers and that action brings its fruits, and urges him not to give up his life.

shots.B12C032S01H01: Vaisampayana says Vyasa speaks again to Yudhishthira, who remains speechless and grieving.
shots.B12C032S01H02: Vyasa says a king must protect subjects and punish transgressors, and that the Kauravas were transgressors who were rightly slain.
shots.B12C032S01H03: Yudhishthira says he does not doubt Vyasa's teaching but still feels burning guilt for having caused so many deaths for the kingdom.
shots.B12C032S01H04: Vyasa asks whether man or the Supreme Being is the doer, argues by the axe example that the cutter is responsible, says acts bear fruit, and urges expiation while alive rather than self-destruction.

B12C033.summary: Yudhishthira laments that he alone caused the deaths of kin, friends and kings, pictures the widows' suffering and his own fall into hell, and asks what life he should now take up. Vyasa answers that Time, through the workings of past acts, took the lives of the fallen, and that killing to save a family or kingdom is no transgression. He recommends the Horse-sacrifice as expiation and urges Yudhishthira to comfort his brothers, install the kin of the fallen on their thrones, and rule.

scenes.B12C033S01: Yudhishthira laments his role in the slaughter, and Vyasa answers that Time caused the deaths and urges the Horse-sacrifice and good rule.

shots.B12C033S01H01: Yudhishthira laments that he alone caused the deaths of kin and kings, pictures the suffering of the widows and his own fall to hell, and asks what life he should take up.
shots.B12C033S01H02: Vaisampayana says Vyasa reflects for a while and then addresses Yudhishthira.
shots.B12C033S01H03: Vyasa says Time, not the Pandavas, took the lives of the fallen, that slaying to save a family or kingdom is no transgression, that the Horse-sacrifice expiates the guilt, and that Yudhishthira should comfort his brothers, seat the fallen men's kin on their thrones, and rule.

B12C034.summary: Yudhishthira asks which acts make a man liable to expiation and which acts free him from sin. Vyasa lists many lapses, such as waking after sunrise, marrying out of turn, killing a Brahmin and selling Vedic knowledge. He then names acts that carry no sin, such as striking down an armed Brahmin who attacks with intent to kill, or lying or stealing for a teacher in distress. The list sets up the rules of expiation that follow.

scenes.B12C034S01: Vyasa lists the lapses that require expiation and the acts that carry no sin, answering Yudhishthira's question.

shots.B12C034S01H01: Yudhishthira asks what acts make a man liable to expiation and what acts free him from sin.
shots.B12C034S01H02: Vyasa lists lapses that need expiation, including killing a Brahmin and selling Vedic knowledge, then names acts done in self-defence, for a preceptor, or to save life that carry no sin.

B12C035.summary: Vyasa describes the expiations for sin: years of mendicant austerity, gifts of cattle and wealth to Brahmins, fasts, and the great Horse-sacrifice. He prescribes penances for lesser faults, and says deliberate sins are graver than accidental ones. He notes that expiations are meant for believers and not the faithless, and urges Yudhishthira to atone through right conduct rather than take his own life.

scenes.B12C035S01: Vyasa describes the expiations for killing a Brahmin and other sins, and urges Yudhishthira to atone and not give up his life.

shots.B12C035S01H01: Vyasa lists penances such as twelve years of mendicancy, gifts of cattle and wealth, fasts and the Horse-sacrifice, says all sins but the gravest can be expiated, and urges Yudhishthira to act rightly rather than give up his life.
shots.B12C035S01H02: Vaisampayana says Yudhishthira reflects briefly and then replies to the sage.

B12C036.summary: Yudhishthira asks which food is clean, which gifts are praiseworthy, and who deserves a gift. Vyasa recounts Manu's discourse to a company of Rishis, which classes some foods as forbidden for Brahmins and some gifts as worthless or harmful. Manu holds that a gift to an unlearned Brahmin is wasted and that a bad gift harms both giver and receiver. The chapter gives rules on giving that match the expiation teaching before it.

scenes.B12C036S01: Vyasa passes on Manu's teaching on clean and forbidden food and on whom it is proper to give to.

shots.B12C036S01H01: Yudhishthira asks what food is clean, what gifts are praiseworthy, and who deserves them.
shots.B12C036S01H02: Vyasa recounts Manu's teaching to the Rishis on what food to eat, which foods and sources are forbidden to Brahmins, and that gifts to unlearned or unworthy persons are wasted or harmful.

B12C037.summary: Yudhishthira asks to hear the duties of kings and of all four orders, and how virtue can be reconciled with kingship. Vyasa directs him to Bhishma, the aged Kuru grandsire who knows the duties of kings. Yudhishthira objects that he cannot approach Bhishma after having had him slain by deceit, but Krishna urges him to accept his duty. Yudhishthira agrees and enters the city in a grand procession.

scenes.B12C037S01: Vyasa directs Yudhishthira to Bhishma for counsel; Yudhishthira objects, and Krishna urges him to accept his duty.
scenes.B12C037S02: Yudhishthira is persuaded and enters the city in a grand procession, welcomed by the citizens.

shots.B12C037S01H01: Yudhishthira asks to hear the duties of kings and of all four orders, and how he can reconcile virtue with kingly duty.
shots.B12C037S01H02: Vaisampayana says Vyasa directs Yudhishthira to Bhishma, the old Kuru grandsire, and lists Bhishma's learning and teachers, and Yudhishthira replies to Vyasa.
shots.B12C037S01H03: Yudhishthira objects that he cannot approach Bhishma after having had him slain by deceit.
shots.B12C037S01H04: Vaisampayana says Krishna, moved to benefit all the four orders, addresses the king.
shots.B12C037S01H05: Krishna urges Yudhishthira to stop his grief, obey Vyasa, and heed the Brahmins, his brothers and the people.
shots.B12C037S02H01: Yudhishthira, persuaded by Krishna, Vyasa and others, sets out, and the procession enters the city in splendour, with the citizens cheering and the streets decked out.

B12C038.summary: As the Pandavas enter the city, crowds and women praise them and Draupadi, and Yudhishthira blesses the Brahmins with gifts. A Rakshasa named Charvaka, disguised as a mendicant and a friend of Duryodhana, publicly accuses Yudhishthira of killing kin and urges him to give up his life. The Brahmins expose Charvaka as the Rakshasa, and their utterance kills him on the spot.

scenes.B12C038S01: Yudhishthira is welcomed into the city, but the disguised Rakshasa Charvaka accuses him and is slain by the Brahmins' power.

shots.B12C038S01H01: The city welcomes the Pandavas and Draupadi with praise, Yudhishthira worships and gives gifts to Brahmins, and then the disguised Rakshasa Charvaka, a friend of Duryodhana, steps forward.
shots.B12C038S01H02: Charvaka tells Yudhishthira that the Brahmins call him a wicked slayer of kin and urges him to give up his life.
shots.B12C038S01H03: Yudhishthira begs the Brahmins not to scorn him and says he will soon give up his life.
shots.B12C038S01H04: The Brahmins say they said no such thing, and by their spiritual sight they expose the speaker as the Rakshasa Charvaka, friend of Duryodhana.
shots.B12C038S01H05: The enraged Brahmins utter a sacred sound that kills Charvaka, and they leave after blessing Yudhishthira.

B12C039.summary: Krishna tells Yudhishthira to honour Brahmins, and explains that the Rakshasa Charvaka had won a boon that protected him from every creature except those he offended, the Brahmins. Brahma had arranged that Charvaka would befriend Duryodhana, insult the Brahmins, and be destroyed by their curse. Krishna urges Yudhishthira not to grieve for kin who died in their duties, and to protect his subjects and worship Brahmins.

scenes.B12C039S01: Krishna explains that Charvaka was doomed by his own boon and urges Yudhishthira to rule well and honour Brahmins.

shots.B12C039S01H01: Krishna tells Yudhishthira to honour Brahmins, explains that Charvaka's boon was undone by offending them, and urges him not to grieve and to rule well.

B12C040.summary: Yudhishthira takes his seat on a golden throne, surrounded by Krishna, Satyaki, his brothers, Kunti and the elders. Priests perform the coronation rites, and Krishna and Dhritarashtra pour sanctified water over the new king's head. The people bring gifts and the Brahmins bless him, and he rewards them and is installed as king of the restored realm.

scenes.B12C040S01: Yudhishthira is anointed as king with sacred water, receives blessings and gifts from people and Brahmins, and is installed on the throne.

shots.B12C040S01H01: Yudhishthira takes his golden seat with his family and elders around him, the priests perform the coronation rites, Krishna and Dhritarashtra pour sanctified water over him, and Brahmins bless him in return for gifts.

B12C041.summary: Yudhishthira tells his subjects that Dhritarashtra is his father and god, and asks them to serve the old king as before, since he lives for him alone. He dismisses the citizens and assigns offices: Bhima as heir apparent, Vidura as counsellor, Sanjaya over finance, Nakula over the army, Arjuna over the forces, Dhaumya as priest, and Sahadeva at his side. He also tells Vidura and Yuyutsu to carry out Dhritarashtra's wishes.

scenes.B12C041S01: Yudhishthira tells his people to honour Dhritarashtra, and appoints his brothers and ministers to government posts.

shots.B12C041S01H01: Yudhishthira declares Dhritarashtra his father and god, asks his subjects to serve him, dismisses the citizens, and assigns offices to Bhima, Vidura, Sanjaya, Nakula, Arjuna, Dhaumya and Sahadeva.

B12C042.summary: Yudhishthira performs funeral rites for each of his fallen kinsmen and allies, and Dhritarashtra gives gifts for his sons' sake. The king gives wealth to Brahmins in the names of Drona, Karna, Abhimanyu, Ghatotkacha, Virata, Drupada and others, and founds food-halls, water-places and tanks in their memory. He honours Dhritarashtra, Gandhari and Vidura, and cares for the widows, the blind and the destitute, and then enjoys peace.

scenes.B12C042S01: Yudhishthira performs funeral rites and gifts for the fallen, cares for their families, and honours the elders.

shots.B12C042S01H01: Yudhishthira and Dhritarashtra perform funeral rites and charity for the fallen, the king founds food-halls and tanks in their names, and cares for widows, the blind and the destitute.

B12C043.summary: Yudhishthira thanks Krishna for restoring his ancestral kingdom and praises him in a long hymn. He calls Krishna Vishnu, Hari, the creator and dissolver of the universe, and names him by countless forms and titles. Pleased by the hymn, Krishna begins to speak warmly to the king.

scenes.B12C043S01: Yudhishthira praises Krishna with a long hymn of thanks, and Krishna is pleased.

shots.B12C043S01H01: Yudhishthira thanks Krishna for regaining the kingdom and hymns him by many names and forms, and Krishna is pleased and begins to speak kindly to him.

B12C044.summary: Yudhishthira sends the people home and asks his brothers to rest after their wounds and exile. He gives each brother a palace that once belonged to a Kaurava prince: Bhima takes Duryodhana's, Arjuna Dussasana's, Nakula Durmarshana's, and Sahadeva Durmukha's. The counsellors return to their homes, and Krishna retires with Satyaki to Arjuna's palace, where all feast and sleep.

scenes.B12C044S01: Yudhishthira rests his brothers and assigns them the palaces of the Kaurava princes.

shots.B12C044S01H01: Yudhishthira sends the people home and asks his brothers to rest, then gives each brother a former Kaurava palace, while Krishna and Satyaki take Arjuna's palace, and all feast and sleep.

B12C045.summary: Janamejaya asks what Yudhishthira did after regaining his kingdom, and what Krishna did next. Vaisampayana says Yudhishthira gives gifts to Brahmins, servants and guests, and honours his elders, Kripa, Vidura, Yuyutsu and Dhritarashtra. He then goes to Krishna and finds him seated in deep meditation, and speaks to him gently, but Krishna does not answer.

scenes.B12C045S01: Janamejaya asks what happened next, and Vaisampayana describes Yudhishthira's generosity and his visit to Krishna, who sits in meditation.

shots.B12C045S01H01: Janamejaya asks Vaisampayana what Yudhishthira did after regaining his kingdom and what Krishna did after that.
shots.B12C045S01H02: Vaisampayana says Yudhishthira gives gifts to Brahmins, servants and guests, honours his elders, and then approaches Krishna, who is seated in deep meditation and does not answer him.

B12C046.summary: Yudhishthira asks Krishna why he is so still in meditation. Krishna says Bhishma, lying on his bed of arrows, is thinking of him, and that he had been concentrating on Bhishma in return. He urges Yudhishthira to go and learn the duties of kings from Bhishma before he dies, and Yudhishthira agrees. Krishna's chariot is then readied for the journey.

scenes.B12C046S01: Yudhishthira asks Krishna about his stillness, and Krishna explains that Bhishma's wisdom must be learned before he dies; the chariot is then readied.

shots.B12C046S01H01: Yudhishthira marvels at Krishna's stillness and asks its cause.
shots.B12C046S01H02: Krishna says Bhishma, on his bed of arrows, is thinking of him, recalls Bhishma's deeds and learning, and urges Yudhishthira to question him before he dies; Yudhishthira agrees.
shots.B12C046S01H03: Satyaki has Krishna's chariot yoked, and Daruka reports that it is ready.

B12C047.summary: Janamejaya asks how Bhishma, lying on his bed of arrows, gave up his body and what yoga he followed. Vaisampayana describes how, at the sun's northward turn, Bhishma drew his soul inward while many sages, including Vyasa and Narada, sat around him. Bhishma hymned Krishna at great length as the Supreme Being, the creator and dissolver of all things, and Krishna granted him heavenly knowledge before departing with the others.

scenes.B12C047S01: Bhishma prepares to die at the northern turn of the sun, hymns Krishna at length, and receives heavenly knowledge; Krishna and the others then depart.

shots.B12C047S01H01: Janamejaya asks how the Kuru grandsire, lying on his bed of arrows, gave up his body and what yoga he followed.
shots.B12C047S01H02: Vaisampayana says that at the sun's northward turn Bhishma drew his soul inward, surrounded by many sages including Vyasa and Narada, and then hymned Vasudeva with joined palms.
shots.B12C047S01H03: Bhishma hymns Krishna at great length, calling him the Supreme Being, the creator and dissolver of the universe, worshipped under countless forms and names.
shots.B12C047S01H04: Krishna grants Bhishma heavenly knowledge and departs; the sages praise both, and Krishna and the Pandavas ride away in their chariots, greeted by the people.

B12C048.summary: Krishna, Yudhishthira and the others ride to Kurukshetra, where the battlefield is still strewn with bones and remains. Krishna points out the lakes of Rama, son of Jamadagni, where Rama is said to have offered Kshatriya blood to his ancestors after destroying the Kshatriyas. Yudhishthira doubts the story and asks how the Kshatriya order could have been wiped out and then revived, and Krishna sets out to explain it.

scenes.B12C048S01: The party crosses the battlefield of Kurukshetra, Krishna recalls Rama's destruction of the Kshatriyas, and Yudhishthira asks how the order was revived.

shots.B12C048S01H01: Vaisampayana says Krishna, Yudhishthira and the others ride to the battlefield, which is strewn with bones, and Krishna points out Rama's five lakes where Rama offered Kshatriya blood to his ancestors.
shots.B12C048S01H02: Yudhishthira doubts that Rama thrice exterminated the Kshatriyas and asks how the order could be destroyed and then regrow.
shots.B12C048S01H03: Vaisampayana says Krishna then gives Yudhishthira the full account of how the earth came to be filled with Kshatriyas again.

B12C049.summary: Krishna tells Yudhishthira how Rama, son of Jamadagni, came to destroy the Kshatriyas. A mix-up of sacred food shapes the family line, and Rama gets a great axe from Mahadeva. After the sons of Arjuna, the Haihaya king, kill his father Jamadagni, Rama wipes out the Kshatriyas many times over, until Kasyapa takes the earth and the surviving Kshatriyas, hidden among herders and others, are restored as kings.

scenes.B12C049S01: Krishna begins Rama's story with the lineage of Kusika and Gadhi and the swap of sacred food that gave Satyavati a fierce son, and her argument with her husband Richika.
scenes.B12C049S02: Krishna tells how Rama destroyed the Kshatriyas, how Kasyapa took the earth, and how the hidden Kshatriya survivors were installed as kings.

shots.B12C049S01H01: Krishna begins to tell how Rama, son of Jamadagni, destroyed the Kshatriyas, and traces the royal line through Kusika and Gadhi to the swap of sacred food meant for Satyavati and her mother.
shots.B12C049S01H02: Richika tells Satyavati that the swap has caused a fierce son to be conceived, and that her son will be a Brahmin.
shots.B12C049S01H03: Satyavati replies that Richika could create other worlds, and asks him to give her a righteous and peaceful son.
shots.B12C049S01H04: Richika says he has never lied, that the outcome was fixed by destiny, and that all of Satyavati's descendants will have Brahmanic virtues.
shots.B12C049S01H05: Satyavati asks that her grandson be such a man, but that she have a son of tranquil pursuits.
shots.B12C049S02H01: Richika says there is no real difference between a son and a grandson, and agrees to her wish.
shots.B12C049S02H02: Krishna recounts that Satyavati bore Jamadagni, whose son Rama took an axe from Mahadeva; the sons of Arjuna killed Jamadagni, Rama then slaughtered the Kshatriyas many times over, and Kasyapa took the earth.
shots.B12C049S02H03: The Earth speaks to Kasyapa, naming Kshatriyas hidden among women, bears, herders and others, and asks him to restore them as protectors.
shots.B12C049S02H04: Krishna says Kasyapa installed those hidden Kshatriyas as kings, and that the present Kshatriya families descend from them.
shots.B12C049S02H05: Vaisampayana says Krishna continues on his chariot after speaking with Yudhishthira, shining like the sun.

B12C050.summary: Yudhishthira is amazed at Rama's deeds, and Krishna and Yudhishthira go to Bhishma lying on his bed of arrows on the banks of the Oghavati, surrounded by sages. Krishna asks whether Bhishma's mind is still clear, praises his mastery over death and his learning in all the duties, and urges him to dispel Yudhishthira's grief. Bhishma hymns Krishna, who reveals his divine form and tells Bhishma that fifty-six days remain before he will depart at the sun's northward turn, and that he should instruct Yudhishthira.

scenes.B12C050S01: Krishna and Yudhishthira visit Bhishma, Krishna praises him and asks him to comfort Yudhishthira, Bhishma hymns Krishna, and Krishna reveals his form and sets the time of Bhishma's death.

shots.B12C050S01H01: Yudhishthira marvels at Rama's feats, and Krishna and Yudhishthira go to Bhishma on the Oghavati banks, where sages sit around him.
shots.B12C050S01H02: Krishna asks Bhishma whether his mind is still clear, notes his mastery over death, praises his learning in every branch of duty, and asks him to comfort Yudhishthira.
shots.B12C050S01H03: Vaisampayana says Bhishma raises his head a little and speaks with joined hands.
shots.B12C050S01H04: Bhishma hymns Krishna as the origin and dissolution of all the worlds, and asks for what is good for him.
shots.B12C050S01H05: Krishna says he showed his form because of Bhishma's devotion, tells him fifty-six days of life remain before he departs at the sun's northward turn, and urges him to instruct Yudhishthira.

B12C051.summary: Bhishma replies that his pain and weakness leave him unable to speak in Krishna's presence, and asks Krishna to instruct Yudhishthira himself. Krishna grants Bhishma a boon that keeps his mind and memory clear and frees him from pain and confusion. The sages worship Krishna, heavenly flowers fall, and the company leaves at sunset for the city.

scenes.B12C051S01: Bhishma asks Krishna to speak for him, Krishna grants him a boon of clear mind and freedom from pain, and the company leaves at sunset.

shots.B12C051S01H01: Vaisampayana says Bhishma replies to Krishna's words.
shots.B12C051S01H02: Bhishma, weakened by pain, says he cannot speak in Krishna's presence and asks Krishna to instruct Yudhishthira.
shots.B12C051S01H03: Krishna grants Bhishma a boon that pain, confusion and hunger will not overcome him, that his memory and understanding will stay clear, and that he will have celestial sight.
shots.B12C051S01H04: The sages worship Krishna, heavenly flowers fall, and at sunset the sages and the Pandavas take their leave for the city.

B12C052.summary: Krishna wakes before dawn, performs his rites, and gives a thousand cows to Brahmins. He sends Satyaki to ask Yudhishthira whether the king is ready to visit Bhishma. Yudhishthira asks that no soldiers accompany them, so that Bhishma's last teaching is not crowded out, and the party drives out to the bed of arrows.

scenes.B12C052S01: Krishna prepares for the visit, sends Satyaki to Yudhishthira, and they drive out without an army to see Bhishma.

shots.B12C052S01H01: Krishna wakes before dawn, performs his rites and gifts, and sends Satyaki to ask Yudhishthira whether he is ready to go to Bhishma.
shots.B12C052S01H02: Yudhishthira asks for his chariot, says no soldiers should come, and notes that Bhishma will soon speak of great mysteries and should not be crowded.
shots.B12C052S01H03: Vaisampayana says the Pandavas join Krishna, and with Satyaki they drive to Bhishma, greet the sages, and approach the bed of arrows.

B12C053.summary: Janamejaya asks what was said when Bhishma lay on his bed of arrows. Narada urges the Pandavas to question Bhishma before he dies, and Yudhishthira asks Krishna to speak first. Krishna asks after Bhishma's health, and Bhishma says his pain has gone and his memory is clear through Krishna's favour. Krishna answers that Bhishma's fame must be enhanced, and urges him to teach Yudhishthira as a father teaches his sons.

scenes.B12C053S01: Narada urges the Pandavas to question Bhishma, Krishna asks about his health, and Krishna urges Bhishma to teach Yudhishthira.

shots.B12C053S01H01: Janamejaya asks what was discussed when Bhishma lay on his bed of arrows with the Pandavas around him.
shots.B12C053S01H02: Vaisampayana says Narada and others gather, Narada urges the Pandavas to ask Bhishma before he dies, and Yudhishthira asks Krishna to speak first.
shots.B12C053S01H03: Krishna asks Bhishma whether he passed the night well and whether his pain and confusion have eased.
shots.B12C053S01H04: Bhishma says his pain has left him, that through Krishna's grace he knows past, present and future and the branches of duty, and asks why Krishna does not teach Yudhishthira himself.
shots.B12C053S01H05: Krishna says he will enhance Bhishma's fame, that Bhishma's words will carry the weight of the Vedas, and urges him to teach Yudhishthira as a father teaches his sons.

B12C054.summary: Bhishma agrees to teach, saying his mind is steady through Krishna's grace, and asks Yudhishthira to question him freely. Krishna notes that Yudhishthira is too ashamed to approach, given the slaughter he caused. Bhishma defends the Kshatriya duty of fighting, even against kin and teachers in an unjust battle, and says a righteous battle brings heaven and fame. Yudhishthira bows at his feet, and Bhishma invites him to ask without fear.

scenes.B12C054S01: Bhishma agrees to speak, defends the Kshatriya duty to fight, even against kin in unjust battle, and invites Yudhishthira to ask.

shots.B12C054S01H01: Bhishma agrees to discourse, says his speech and mind are steady, and asks Yudhishthira to question him, praising the king's virtues.
shots.B12C054S01H02: Krishna says Yudhishthira is too ashamed to approach Bhishma, having caused a great slaughter of those he should have honoured.
shots.B12C054S01H03: Bhishma says a Kshatriya's duty is to fight, even to slay kin and teachers in an unjust battle, and that a righteous battle brings heaven and fame.
shots.B12C054S01H04: Yudhishthira bows at Bhishma's feet, is welcomed with affection, and Bhishma tells him to ask without fear.

B12C055.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to teach the duties of kings, which he calls the highest science and the reins that hold the world together. Bhishma tells him to honour gods and Brahmins, to act with prompt exertion rather than rely on destiny, and to keep to truth. He teaches that a king must be neither too mild nor too fierce, that Brahmins should be banished rather than physically punished, and that a king should care for his subjects as a mother cares for her child. He warns that servants who grow too familiar with the king will disrespect him.

scenes.B12C055S01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma about kingly duties, and Bhishma teaches exertion, truth, moderation and care of subjects, with warnings about over-familiarity.

shots.B12C055S01H01: Vaisampayana says Yudhishthira, after bowing to Krishna and taking leave of the elders, begins his questions to Bhishma.
shots.B12C055S01H02: Yudhishthira calls kingly duties the highest science and the reins of the world, and asks Bhishma to speak on them first.
shots.B12C055S01H03: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira to honour gods and Brahmins, to act with prompt exertion, to keep to truth, and to be neither too mild nor too fierce.
shots.B12C055S01H04: Bhishma says Brahmins should be banished rather than physically punished, that a king should treat subjects as a mother her child, and that servants who grow too familiar with the king will disrespect him.

B12C056.summary: Bhishma insists that a king must be ready for action, making peace or war as the situation requires. He gives examples of severe discipline, such as Sagara exiling his son Asamanjas and Uddalaka casting off Swetaketu, and advises the king to keep his counsels secret and to employ honest servants. He governs with justice and generosity, and describes the best king as one whose subjects live without fear.

scenes.B12C056S01: Bhishma urges a king to act with vigour and justice, gives examples of severe discipline, and describes the qualities of a good king.

shots.B12C056S01H01: Bhishma tells Yudhishthira that a king must be ready for action, gives examples of severe discipline, advises secrecy and trusted servants, and describes the best king as one whose subjects live without fear.

B12C057.summary: Bhishma says protecting subjects is the core of kingly duty, as Vrihaspati and other sages teach, and lists the means of protection: spies, fair taxation, honest officers, fortifications and care of allies. He says exertion is the root of kingly duty, and that a king must be candid yet sometimes shrewd in policy. He declares he has taught only part of the subject, and the listeners praise him, while Yudhishthira promises to ask more the next day.

scenes.B12C057S01: Bhishma stresses protecting subjects and exertion, lists the methods of protection, and says he has taught only part of kingly duty.

shots.B12C057S01H01: Bhishma says protecting subjects is the essence of kingly duty, lists its means from spies and fair taxes to honest officers and fortifications, and says exertion is the root of kingly duty.
shots.B12C057S01H02: Vyasa and the others praise Bhishma, Yudhishthira promises to ask more the next day, and the company bathes, makes evening offerings and returns to the city.

B12C058.summary: Yudhishthira asks why one man should rule the whole world when all men are alike in body and mind. Bhishma explains that in the first age there was no king or punishment, but greed, anger and error spread until the Vedas and righteousness declined, and the gods turned to Brahma. Brahma composed a great treatise on the science of chastisement, later abridged by Shiva, Indra, Brihaspati and Kavi, and the chapter traces its transmission to Vena, a tyrant slain by the sages, and to Prithu, the first true king, from whose rule kingship and its honour are said to come.

scenes.B12C058S01: Bhishma recounts the origin of kingship: a decline into disorder, Brahma's treatise on punishment, the tyrant Vena, and the first true king Prithu.

shots.B12C058S01H01: Vaisampayana says the Pandavas and Yadavas ride out the next morning to Bhishma, greet the sages, and Yudhishthira worships Bhishma and asks his question.
shots.B12C058S01H02: Yudhishthira asks why one man should rule the whole world, what the word king means, and why the whole world bows to one man.
shots.B12C058S01H03: Bhishma recounts how disorder spread in the first age until the gods sought Brahma, who composed the treatise on punishment, which was abridged by later sages and passed to Vena, whose tyranny ended with the birth of the first true king, Prithu, who levelled the earth and was honoured by the gods.
shots.B12C058S01H04: Bhishma says the treatise covered every subject, that since then the learned have held a king no different from a god, and asks which subject Yudhishthira wants to hear next.

B12C059.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to set out the general and special duties of each of the four orders. Bhishma lists nine duties shared by all, then the duties of Brahmins (self-restraint and Vedic study), Kshatriyas (giving without begging, protecting subjects and fighting robbers), Vaisyas (gifts, study, sacrifice and fair earnings from herding and trade), and Sudras (service to the higher orders, with minor sacrifices). He concludes that sacrifice and devotion belong to every order, with the Brahmin foremost.

scenes.B12C059S01: Bhishma gives the general and specific duties of the four orders, ending with the claim that sacrifice belongs to all.

shots.B12C059S01H01: Yudhishthira asks the general and special duties of each order, which modes of life suit each, the duties of kings, the means by which kingdoms grow, and what a king should avoid.
shots.B12C059S01H02: Bhishma lists nine common duties, then the duties of Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaisyas and Sudras, and concludes that sacrifice and devotion belong to every order, with the Brahmin foremost.

B12C060.summary: Bhishma names the four modes of life, Brahmacharya, Garhasthya, Vanaprastha and Bhaikshya, and sets out the duties of each. The student serves his teacher and studies the Vedas, the householder begets children, keeps faith with his wife and is hospitable, the forest hermit withdraws with the sacred texts, and the mendicant has no fixed home and no attachments. He ends with a verse on the householder's virtues.

scenes.B12C060S01: Bhishma names the four stages of life and outlines the duties of each, from student to forest hermit and mendicant.

shots.B12C060S01H01: Bhishma names the four modes of life, Brahmacharya, Garhasthya, Vanaprastha and Bhaikshya, and sets out the duties of each, from study and service to a teacher through household duty to the mendicant's detachment.

B12C061.summary: Yudhishthira asks for duties suited to men in their own position. Bhishma replies that the four modes of life belong to Brahmins, and that a Brahmin who takes up the callings of other orders is disgraced and bound for hell. He stresses that men act under the influence of Time and their own propensities, and that the study of the Vedas is as worthy as kingly power, farming or trade.

scenes.B12C061S01: Bhishma says the four modes of life belong to Brahmins, that a Brahmin straying into other callings is disgraced, and that all acts are shaped by Time.

shots.B12C061S01H01: Yudhishthira asks for duties suited to men like the Pandavas, which are auspicious, beneficial and approved by all.
shots.B12C061S01H02: Bhishma says the four modes of life are for Brahmins, that a Brahmin who adopts the callings of other orders is disgraced, and that men act under the influence of Time and their propensities.

B12C062.summary: Bhishma says that drawing the bowstring, warfare, farming, trade, herding and service for wages are improper for a Brahmin. A Brahmin who falls from his duties becomes like a Sudra, and gifts to such men bring no merit. He describes the duties of the other orders, and concludes that the Kshatriya's duties underlie all the others, as the elephant's footprint covers the tracks of other animals.

scenes.B12C062S01: Bhishma says what is improper for a Brahmin, and that the Kshatriya's duties underlie all the other duties.

shots.B12C062S01H01: Bhishma lists callings improper for a Brahmin, says a Brahmin who falls from duty becomes like a Sudra, and says gifts to such men bring no merit.
shots.B12C062S01H02: Bhishma describes the duties of the other orders and the modes of life open to Kshatriyas and Vaisyas, and concludes that the Kshatriya's duties underlie all the others.

B12C063.summary: Bhishma argues that all duties, including those of the four modes of life, fall under kingly duty, since disorder in royal duty brings evil on all creatures. He tells how King Mandhatri, seeking to see Narayana, met the god in the form of Indra and asked how to perform his duties. Indra explains that kingly duty came first from the Supreme, contains all other duties, and protected the others when Vishnu destroyed the Asuras, so that Kshatriya duty is the foremost of all.

scenes.B12C063S01: Bhishma tells how Mandhatri met Narayana in the form of Indra, who explained that kingly duties are the foremost of all duties.

shots.B12C063S01H01: Bhishma says all duties, including those of the four modes of life, fall under kingly duty, and tells how Mandhatri performed a sacrifice to see Narayana and Narayana appeared to him as Indra.
shots.B12C063S01H02: Indra asks Mandhatri what he seeks by seeing Narayana, and offers to grant him any other boon.
shots.B12C063S01H03: Mandhatri asks to see the first of gods and to learn how to perform the duties of a Kshatriya.
shots.B12C063S01H04: Indra explains that kingly duties came first from the Supreme, contain all other duties, and revived the eternal duties after Vishnu destroyed the Asuras, so Kshatriya duty is foremost.

B12C064.summary: Indra continues that kings must uphold their duties by reclaiming land, giving gifts, avoiding begging and ruling impartially, and that Brahmins who neglect their own duties should be punished like Sudras. When Mandhatri asks what duties foreign and robber tribes should keep, Indra says they should honour parents, teachers and kings, follow the Vedas, and make gifts. Indra warns that when kingly duty fails, men will fall into disorder and false sects, and honours the king who watches over men's duties. Bhishma closes by saying Narayana departed and that the path of the ancients should be followed.

scenes.B12C064S01: Indra explains that kings must uphold their duties, sets out duties for robber tribes, and warns of decline when kingly rule fails.
scenes.B12C064S02: Bhishma closes by telling Yudhishthira to follow the path set by the ancients.

shots.B12C064S01H01: Indra says Kshatriya duties are foremost, that kings must reclaim land, perform great sacrifices, avoid begging and protect subjects, and that Brahmins who neglect their duties should be treated like Sudras.
shots.B12C064S01H02: Mandhatri asks what duties the foreign and robber tribes should observe, and which duties kings should enforce on them.
shots.B12C064S01H03: Indra says robber tribes should honour parents, teachers and kings, follow the Vedas, dig wells, give water and gifts, and perform the sacrificial offerings.
shots.B12C064S01H04: Mandhatri says wicked men live disguised among all four orders and modes of life.
shots.B12C064S01H05: Indra warns that when kingly duty fails, false sects will multiply and men will go astray, and that he honours the king who watches over men's duties.
shots.B12C064S02H01: Bhishma says Narayana departed, and tells Yudhishthira to keep to the path the ancient kings followed.

B12C065.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to explain the four modes of human life in more detail. Bhishma says a righteous king who rules well, gives gifts, honours the worthy and protects his people earns the merit of every mode of life. He closes by urging Yudhishthira to keep to the king's duty of protection, which he calls the most meritorious of all.

scenes.B12C065S01: Yudhishthira asks about the four modes of life, and Bhishma explains that a king who practises the duties of each mode gains its merit, while protecting subjects is the king's chief task.

shots.B12C065S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma to explain the four modes of human life in detail.
shots.B12C065S01H02: Bhishma says that a just king earns the merit of each mode of life through his conduct, and that protecting the righteous is worth more than the asceticism of forest hermits.
shots.B12C065S01H03: Bhishma closes by telling Yudhishthira that if he keeps to the king's duty of protection, he will gain the merit of all four modes of life and all four orders.

B12C066.summary: Yudhishthira asks what the chief duties of a kingdom are. Bhishma says the first duty is to choose and crown a king, since anarchy leaves a land open to robbers and mutual destruction. He tells how Manu was persuaded to accept kingship in return for a share of the people's wealth and merit, and how a king should carry himself once crowned.

scenes.B12C066S01: Bhishma explains why a king must be crowned, then tells the story of Manu, who was reluctant until the people offered him a share of their produce and merit, and gives advice on how a king should conduct himself.
scenes.B12C066S02: A heading marks the start of the next section, LXVIII.

shots.B12C066S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma what the principal duties of a kingdom are, after hearing about the four modes and orders.
shots.B12C066S01H02: Bhishma says that crowning a king is the first duty, because a kingdom without rule grows weak, is overrun by robbers, and its people devour one another.
shots.B12C066S01H03: Manu, asked to rule, declines because he fears the sins that come with governing a deceitful people.
shots.B12C066S01H04: The people promise Manu a share of their livestock, metals and grain, and a portion of the merit from his protection, and he accepts and sets out to restore order.
shots.B12C066S01H05: Bhishma advises that people should first choose a king, that he should be honoured and well provided for, and that he should speak and act with courtesy.
shots.B12C066S02H01: A heading marks the start of the next section, LXVIII.

B12C067.summary: Yudhishthira asks why Brahmanas call the king a god. Bhishma answers with a teaching that the sage Vrihaspati gave to King Vasumanas of Kosala, in which the king is the root of all duties and the guardian against chaos. Vrihaspati lists the forms a king takes and urges loyalty to him, and Vasumanas accepts the teaching and begins to protect his subjects.

scenes.B12C067S01: Yudhishthira asks about the king's divine status, and Bhishma tells the story of Vrihaspati instructing King Vasumanas on the king's role, the disorder that follows without him, the forms he takes, and the loyalty owed to him.

shots.B12C067S01H01: Yudhishthira asks why the Brahmanas say the king is a god.
shots.B12C067S01H02: Bhishma introduces an old story of the sage Vrihaspati teaching King Vasumanas of Kosala, who approaches him with proper humility.
shots.B12C067S01H03: Vasumanas asks what makes creatures grow or perish, and by what worship they can gain lasting happiness.
shots.B12C067S01H04: Vrihaspati says all duties rest on the king: without his protection the strong would prey on the weak and religion, marriage, learning and trade would collapse, and he names the five forms the king takes and urges loyalty to him, after which Vasumanas begins to protect his subjects.

B12C068.summary: Yudhishthira asks what further duties a king has in defending his realm, handling spies and winning his subjects' trust. Bhishma says a king must first master himself, then gives long practical advice on spies, peace and war, taxation, justice, fortifications and the seven limbs of a state. He ends by arguing that the king's conduct decides which age of the world comes, from the Krita age down to Kali.

scenes.B12C068S01: Bhishma gives detailed advice on self-control, spies, war and peace, justice and defence, and then argues that the king's rule decides which age of the world comes.

shots.B12C068S01H01: Yudhishthira asks what further duties a king has, how he should defend his kingdom and beat his enemies, how to use spies, and how to win the confidence of all his people.
shots.B12C068S01H02: Bhishma says a king must first conquer himself, then gives long advice on spies, peace and war, taxes, justice, fortifications and the seven limbs of a state, and closes with two verses of Vrihaspati.
shots.B12C068S01H03: Yudhishthira asks what benefit the science of chastisement, the king and the subjects each derive from the others.
shots.B12C068S01H04: Bhishma says the science of chastisement keeps each order to its duty, and that the king decides the age: full reliance on it brings the Krita age, while neglect brings the decline into Treta, Dwapara and Kali.

B12C069.summary: Yudhishthira asks whether a king who follows such conduct can gain lasting happiness in this world and the next. Bhishma lists thirty-six virtues a king should practise, such as restraint, kindness, fair taxation, careful punishment and humility towards elders. Vaisampayana ends the chapter by saying Yudhishthira accepted the teaching and ruled by it from then on.

scenes.B12C069S01: Bhishma lists the virtues a good king should practise, and Yudhishthira, taking the teaching to heart, begins to rule by it.

shots.B12C069S01H01: Yudhishthira asks whether a king who follows such conduct can easily gain lasting happiness here and hereafter.
shots.B12C069S01H02: Bhishma lists thirty-six virtues a king should practise, among them restraint, kindness, fair taxation, care in punishment and humility towards seniors, and says a king who keeps them gains great merit.
shots.B12C069S01H03: Vaisampayana says Yudhishthira, eager to learn, honoured his grandsire and began to rule by this teaching.

B12C070.summary: Yudhishthira asks how a king should protect his subjects so that he avoids grief and does not offend against righteousness. Bhishma gives a brief list of duties: honour learned Brahmanas, control lust and anger, collect a fair share of the produce as tax, and never fill the treasury by unrighteous means. He calls the protection of subjects the highest duty of a king, with rewards that only a king can earn.

scenes.B12C070S01: Bhishma briefly sums up the king's eternal duties, including respect for Brahmanas, fair taxation, self-control, and protecting subjects as the highest duty.

shots.B12C070S01H01: Yudhishthira asks how a king should protect his subjects so as to avoid grief and stay within righteousness.
shots.B12C070S01H02: Bhishma briefly lists the king's duties: honour learned Brahmanas, avoid lust and anger, collect a fair sixth of the produce as tax, and treat protecting subjects as the highest duty, whose reward only a king can earn.

B12C071.summary: Bhishma says a king should appoint as his priest someone who protects the good and punishes the wicked. He retells a dialogue between King Pururavas and the wind god Matariswan on the origin of the four orders and whom the earth belongs to. The wind god concludes that the Brahmana holds first place by birth, that the priest shares in the king's merit, and that sacrifice and order depend on a king.

scenes.B12C071S01: Bhishma recommends appointing a priest, then recounts how Pururavas asks the wind god about the origin of the four orders, the Brahmana's precedence and the claim to the earth, and the wind god answers at length.

shots.B12C071S01H01: Bhishma says a king should appoint as his priest someone who protects the good and punishes the wicked, and introduces the tale of Pururavas and the wind god Matariswan.
shots.B12C071S01H02: Pururavas asks where the Brahmana and the other three orders came from, and why the Brahmana is foremost.
shots.B12C071S01H03: Matariswan explains that the four orders sprang from Brahman's mouth, arms, thighs and feet, with the Brahmana to study the Vedas, the Kshatriya to rule, the Vaisya to farm and trade, and the Sudra to serve.
shots.B12C071S01H04: Pururavas asks whether the earth belongs to the Brahmana or to the Kshatriya.
shots.B12C071S01H05: The wind god says everything belongs to the Brahmana by birth, though in times of distress a king may give conquered land to a worthy one, and that the priest shares the king's merit, that sacrifice depends on a king, and that a king is like Indra, Yama and Dharma.

B12C072.summary: Bhishma says a king should choose a learned priest, and that king and priest should be friends so the subjects stay content. Sage Kasyapa tells King Aila that quarrels between Brahmanas and Kshatriyas bring ruin, and that Rudra, the god of destruction, arises in the hearts of sinners and strikes the land. Kasyapa adds that the sinless must keep away from the sinful, and that the next world rewards the righteous and punishes the wicked differently.

scenes.B12C072S01: Bhishma urges a king to appoint a learned priest, and Aila and Kasyapa discuss how quarrels between Brahmanas and Kshatriyas bring ruin and how Rudra is tied to the sins of men.
scenes.B12C072S02: Aila asks why destruction falls on the innocent as well as the guilty, and Kasyapa answers that the sinless should avoid mixing with the sinful.
scenes.B12C072S03: Kasyapa says the next world differs sharply for the righteous and the sinful, and concludes that a king should install a priest and honour Brahmanas.

shots.B12C072S01H01: Bhishma urges a king to appoint a learned priest, says king and priest should be friends for the subjects' happiness, and introduces the talk of Aila and Kasyapa.
shots.B12C072S01H02: Aila asks which of the Brahmana and the Kshatriya is superior when they part ways, and on whom the other orders depend.
shots.B12C072S01H03: Kasyapa says that when the two quarrel the kingdom falls into disorder, with robbers, failed crops and lost learning.
shots.B12C072S01H04: Aila asks where Rudra comes from and what form he takes.
shots.B12C072S01H05: Kasyapa says Rudra dwells in human hearts and destroys the bodies he inhabits and others too, like a violent wind.
shots.B12C072S02H01: Aila observes that wind and rain do not visibly destroy men, but that men are ruined through lust and malice.
shots.B12C072S02H02: Kasyapa compares Rudra's stupefying force to a fire that spreads from one house across a village, striking honest and wicked alike.
shots.B12C072S02H03: Aila asks why men would act well if punishment falls on everyone regardless.
shots.B12C072S02H04: Kasyapa answers that the sinless are caught up when mixed with the sinful, as dry wood burns with wet, so they should keep apart.
shots.B12C072S02H05: Aila points out that the earth, sun, wind and water treat the honest and the wicked alike.
shots.B12C072S03H01: Kasyapa says the world treats the two groups alike but the next world does not, and that a king should install a learned priest and honour Brahmanas.

B12C073.summary: Bhishma says a kingdom's safety rests on the king, and the king's safety rests on his priest. He retells how King Muchukunda, after conquering the earth, met the Lord of Alaka's Rakshasa army, which his priest Vasishtha stopped through penance. Muchukunda refuses to hold sovereignty as a gift and insists on ruling by his own might, and Bhishma concludes that a king who yields precedence to Brahmanas wins fame.

scenes.B12C073S01: Bhishma recounts how King Muchukunda and Vaisravana clash over sovereignty, with the Rakshasa army and the priest Vasishtha in the middle, and Muchukunda's firm answer to the Lord of Alaka.

shots.B12C073S01H01: Bhishma says a kingdom's safety rests on the king and the king's on his priest, and recounts how Muchukunda conquered the earth, then fought Vaisravana's Rakshasas, which Vasishtha halted through penance.
shots.B12C073S01H02: Vaisravana rebukes Muchukunda for relying on Brahmana power, and Muchukunda replies that Brahmanas and Kshatriyas share one origin and each has its own power to protect the people.
shots.B12C073S01H03: Muchukunda declines sovereignty given as a gift and insists on ruling by his own arms, which surprises Vaisravana, and Bhishma concludes that a king who yields precedence to Brahmanas wins fame.

B12C074.summary: Yudhishthira asks how a king can raise his subjects and earn heavenly regions. Bhishma says a king should be generous, protect his people, honour the righteous and share in their merit and their sins. Yudhishthira then declares he would rather give up the kingdom for asceticism, and Bhishma replies that his gentleness does not fit a king, urging him to keep to his duty and rule. Bhishma ends by praising the man who gives relief from fear.

scenes.B12C074S01: Bhishma describes the king's conduct, including protection, generosity and sharing in his subjects' merit and sin, and then Yudhishthira wishes to retire to the forest, which Bhishma rejects in favour of duty.
scenes.B12C074S02: Bhishma says the one who relieves fear is most worthy of heaven and urges Yudhishthira to rule cheerfully, protect the good and punish the wicked.

shots.B12C074S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhishma which conduct helps a king raise his subjects and win regions of felicity in the next world.
shots.B12C074S01H02: Bhishma says the king should be generous, sacrificial, devoted to protecting his people, honour the righteous, be deadly to foes, and takes a fourth share of the merit and sin of his subjects.
shots.B12C074S01H03: Yudhishthira says he values sovereignty only for the merit it brings, and resolves to leave the throne for a life of asceticism in the forest.
shots.B12C074S01H04: Bhishma says Yudhishthira's gentleness and compassion will not suffice for a king, and urges him to follow his father and grandfather and not shrink from duty.
shots.B12C074S01H05: Yudhishthira asks what acts lead to heaven, and what felicity and prosperity follow from them.
