shots.B12C363S95H04: Note 1067: the commentator explains the first line as meaning that the speaker has truly treated the subject.
shots.B12C363S95H05: Note 1068: tasya tasya refers to the senses, pracharah means conduct, and pasyatah means the wise man.
shots.B12C363S96H01: Note 1069: one who only knows the Vedas and keeps celibacy is not a superior Brahmin, since more is needed.
shots.B12C363S96H02: Note 1070: sarvavit is taken as Brahmavit, the contented man is one satisfied with self-knowledge, and K.P. Singha is right on the two negatives.
shots.B12C363S96H03: Note 1071: avidhanat is explained as not following either kindness or its opposite.
shots.B12C363S96H04: Note 1072: kamakantah is explained as lovely through desires.
shots.B12C363S96H05: Note 1073: heaven is Brahma with attributes, tranquillity is Brahma without them, and the Vedas and truth matter only as far as they lead to tranquillity.
shots.B12C363S97H01: Note 1074: both vernacular translators misrender this verse, and the note explains ichchasi, santoshat, sattwam, and manas.
shots.B12C363S97H02: Note 1075: samagrah means fully satisfied with knowledge, and contentment from verse 13 makes up six attributes.
shots.B12C363S97H03: Note 1076: the six must be free of Rajas and Tamas, the three are hearing, reflection, and contemplation, and knowing the Soul within the body brings freedom.
shots.B12C363S97H04: Note 1077: anweti is explained as grows.
shots.B12C363S97H05: Note 1078: the reading saviseshani is preferred, and the note explains vishesha and avishesha in yoga terms.
shots.B12C363S98H01: Note 1079: one who has transcended the gunas disregards the power that their destruction is said to bring.
shots.B12C363S98H02: Note 1080: karyyatam is Prakriti, the active principle, while Purusha is inactive, and the supreme cause is Brahma without attributes.
shots.B12C363S98H03: Note 1081: dwandwani is governed by anushthitah, and the speaker has discussed the subject at length and now treats it briefly.
shots.B12C363S98H04: Note 1082: panchasu means among the five elements, and the commentator shows that bhava, abhava, and time fall within the elements.
shots.B12C363S98H05: Note 1083: the construction is expanded to mean that the earlier elements have qualities that run through the later ones.
shots.B12C363S99H01: Note 1084: uttarah means the three things Avidya, desire, and acts, which the vernacular translators skip.
shots.B12C363S99H02: Note 1085: the soul, invested with avidya and desire, becomes a living creature and acts, and through the results of acts becomes Jivatman.
shots.B12C363S99H03: Note 1086: a difficult verse: one who sees all these states as unstained Chit becomes free of desire through knowledge of the Soul.
shots.B12C363S99H04: Note 1087: the learned yogin is meant, and saririnam means the Soul with a subtle body.
shots.B12C363S99H05: Note 1088: sahitah is nivida, and drisyamanah means realised through instruction and reason though unseen by the eye.
shots.B12C363S100H01: Note 1089: the yogin sees within his own and others' bodies the souls in subtle forms.
shots.B12C363S100H02: Note 1090: yogins control their subtle forms at all times, and can enter other forms at will.
shots.B12C363S100H03: Note 1091: yogins in their subtle bodies roam everywhere, even in the most blissful regions of heaven.
shots.B12C363S100H04: Note 1092: ordinary men also have subtle bodies, and in dreams only the subtle body acts and feels.
shots.B12C363S100H05: Note 1093: the karana bodies are imperishable potentialities that survive even universal destruction and form subtle bodies from past acts.
shots.B12C363S101H01: Note 1094: dhyana is laid down for everyone, not only for renouncers.
shots.B12C363S101H02: Note 1095: pradhanam is Avidya, viniyoga is transformation, and the particle anu means following the scriptures.
shots.B12C363S101H03: Note 1096: the correct reading is ayasaih, made of iron, and the chains are either worldly longings or the bodies men wear.
shots.B12C363S101H04: Note 1097: the dual genitive duhkhayoh is used because worldly pleasure is also pain, and tyajamannah means wishing to give up.
shots.B12C363S101H05: Note 1098: the commentator explains the pronouns of this verse about a growing thing, tying them to desire and to the cause of growth.
shots.B12C363S102H01: Note 1099: uddhriyate means tears up, asina suggests cutting, and the root of the tree is Avidya.
shots.B12C363S102H02: Note 1100: the body is a city, the understanding its mistress, the mind her servant, and the senses its citizens, and acts done to cherish them carry the faults of Rajas and Tamas.
shots.B12C363S102H03: Note 1101: the senses, mind, and understanding all arise from acts, and so rest on them and draw sustenance from them.
shots.B12C363S102H04: Note 1102: the first line of verse 14 is expanded to make its meaning clear.
shots.B12C363S102H05: Note 1103: the soul is stained when the understanding is afflicted, like an image placed upon a mirror.
shots.B12C363S103H01: Note 1104: the son had not yet obtained the light of full knowledge.
shots.B12C363S103H02: Note 1105: the Burdwan version gives eight qualities rather than ten, and a misprint in the Bengal texts causes the trouble; K.P. Singha is correct.
shots.B12C363S103H03: Note 1106: the Rishis regarded an entity as the sum of its properties and not as an unknown substance in which properties inhere.
shots.B12C363S103H04: Note 1107: there are five elements with fifty properties, plus five special properties of the understanding, making sixty.
shots.B12C363S103H05: Note 1108: a difficult verse in which Bhishma asks Yudhishthira to attend to the way of attaining Brahma more than to theories of origin.
shots.B12C363S104H01: Note 1109: the warriors could be slain only by equal opponents who fought them, so they were very superior men.
shots.B12C363S104H02: Note 1110: for gods and Rishis, thinking and summoning are the same.
shots.B12C363S104H03: Note 1111: the accusatives in the first line of verse 5 are governed by hareyam in the previous verse.
shots.B12C363S104H04: Note 1112: a padmaka is a number of ten digits, a thousand million.
shots.B12C363S104H05: Note 1113: living in the woods with the deer, as Madhavi did, confers great merit.
shots.B12C363S105H01: Note 1114: Death is to attain the status of all-pervading Brahma, a boon the Self-born grants to allay her fears.
shots.B12C363S105H02: Note 1115: the phrase means freed from wrath and aversion.
shots.B12C363S105H03: Note 1116: the note cites Vasishtha's question what dharma is, answered first by what accords with the Srutis and Smritis, and then by the conduct of the good.
shots.B12C363S105H04: Note 1117: the translator notes that some lies are excused by many, such as the lie that saved a prince, and that the Rishis wrote for men and not angels.
shots.B12C363S105H05: Note 1118: the commentator says verse 9 refers to the robbed thief who goes to the king to seek justice.
shots.B12C363S106H01: Note 1119: one should not be intoxicated with might or break the eternal ban on taking what belongs to another, and K.P. Singha misrenders this line.
shots.B12C363S106H02: Note 1120: such a man is always alive to his own faults and does not accuse others of what he might do himself.
shots.B12C363S106H03: Note 1121: K.P. Singha misrenders this line.
shots.B12C363S106H04: Note 1122: the construction is simple, and the saying is a form of the golden rule, to do to others as one would have them do to oneself.
shots.B12C363S106H05: Note 1123: the Burdwan version of the second line is wrong, and the note explains the grammar of yad, anyasya, tatah, and kuryat.
shots.B12C363S107H01: Note 1124: a surplus should not be coveted for its own sake but only for such use.
shots.B12C363S107H02: Note 1125: K.P. Singha renders the second line incorrectly.
shots.B12C363S107H03: Priyabhyupagatam is taken as gained through pleasure, not through harm.
shots.B12C363S107H04: The translator is unsure of the sense and reports the commentator's reading that Yudhishthira faults Bhishma's earlier account of the signs of righteousness.
shots.B12C363S107H05: The commentator argues that beings seem to be born, live and die by their own nature, so nature rather than the Vedic texts looks like the cause.
shots.B12C363S108H01: Distress takes endless forms, so the departures from duty it justifies cannot all be listed in any moral code.
shots.B12C363S108H02: Sudras who hear forbidden texts for merit sin, while Brahmanas like Agastya gain merit by cursing, so good conduct is hard to pin down.
shots.B12C363S108H03: The commentator's example is Indra stopping Janamejaya's horse sacrifice, which the king meant to perform for merit.
shots.B12C363S108H04: Gandharva-cities in the sky appear and vanish, which compares sacrifices that look attractive but prove transitory under examination.
shots.B12C363S108H05: The verse shows how hard it is to say who the good are whose conduct should set the standard.
shots.B12C363S109H01: The commentator names Drona and similar men, and asks how their conduct can count as righteous when the good are hard to know.
shots.B12C363S109H02: Viswamitra gained fame through weapons, Jamadagnya lost his Brahmana status by taking up arms, and Vasishtha lost nothing while punishing Viswamitra.
shots.B12C363S109H03: Righteousness does not rest on the Srutis, the Smritis or happiness; its standard is what the learned of old called righteous.
shots.B12C363S109H04: The phrase in this connection refers back to the true cause that governs happiness and its opposite.
shots.B12C363S109H05: A sage whose gross body stayed in the water roved the world in his subtle body by Yoga power.
shots.B12C363S110H01: Criya is explained by the commentator as the possession of Vedic lore.
shots.B12C363S110H02: Jajali began a new vow of travelling the whole earth and sleeping wherever evening found him.
shots.B12C363S110H03: A Beniya's shop is a general store with spices, drugs and nearly every household article.
shots.B12C363S110H04: Bhandajivanah is a person who puts capital to work and lives on the profit.
shots.B12C363S110H05: Charin is taken to mean wandering in search of food.
shots.B12C363S111H01: Some Bengal texts have a three-line verse, while the Bombay edition leaves out the third line.
shots.B12C363S111H02: The commentator reads the second line as explaining what morality with its mysteries is.
shots.B12C363S111H03: Padmaka is the lotus rootstock and also a medicinal wood, Tunga is either lotus filaments or a tree, and the Bombay reading looks wrong.
shots.B12C363S111H04: Weighing all creatures equally, the speaker says a Brahmana does not outweigh a Chandala, nor an elephant a dog.
shots.B12C363S111H05: Variety in the world is compared to the many aspects of the sky, all showing one Godhead.
shots.B12C363S112H01: Devairapihita-dwarah means people whose senses were closed by the gods, that is, defective or lost senses.
shots.B12C363S112H02: The state of Brahma is fearless and has no return, which is why it is called the fearless place.
shots.B12C363S112H03: The mention of sons and grandsons shows that family practices, if not very cruel, carry authority.
shots.B12C363S112H04: Eternal righteousness in the Vedas may be stained by errors, and wise people avoid those errors while fools give up righteousness altogether.
shots.B12C363S112H05: The word iha is the only sign that the speaker means the union of relatives in this world.
shots.B12C363S113H01: K.P. Singha omits half a line, and the Burdwan translator misreads krosatah, which refers to the roaring fire.
shots.B12C363S113H02: Both vernacular translations misunderstand this verse.
shots.B12C363S113H03: Men seeking limited happiness are set against the wise, who seek endless felicity and practise it for Brahma.
shots.B12C363S113H04: Padashinah refers to the gods, who lose track of the man who has passed beyond even the highest regions.
shots.B12C363S113H05: Bhuta means Brahma and Bhavya means heaven, and the Vedas prescribe both kinds of duty.
shots.B12C363S114H01: The commentator cites conflicting rules on killing cows, which makes the subject of duty confused.
shots.B12C363S114H02: Badha is taken as striking or beating, and the verses are read as a protest against slavery.
shots.B12C363S114H03: Some texts tell of Prishadhara killing a cow by mistake for a tiger.
shots.B12C363S114H04: The cow is called mother for her nourishing milk, and the bull is Prajapati for helping create offspring and food.
shots.B12C363S114H05: Nahusha killed a cow and bull to honour the Rishis, who cleansed him, and the sin was spread among females as periodic impurity.
shots.B12C363S115H01: A section heading, SECTION CCCLI, marks the start of the next part.
shots.B12C363S115H02: The Rishis spoke to Nahusha harshly though he had not meant the killing, showing how serious a deliberate act would be.
shots.B12C363S115H03: Sacrifices that harm animals and plants belong to Kshatriyas, while Brahmanas should perform only the sacrifice of Yoga.
shots.B12C363S115H04: Sacrifices attract through fame and need wealth, and the pursuit of wealth leads to many wrongs.
shots.B12C363S115H05: In former times sacrifice was done without desire for fruit, and crops and plants grew without tillage.
shots.B12C363S116H01: Being bereft of wisdom is glossed as failing to attain liberation.
shots.B12C363S116H02: The verse is terse; the translator follows the commentator, finds that reading far-fetched, and offers a view of a Brahmana who acts only as an instrument.
shots.B12C363S116H03: Sacrifices done from duty count even if incomplete, while fruit-seeking sacrifices need expiation when blocked.
shots.B12C363S116H04: Swayajna means sacrifice in oneself, and the Brahman of the Veda is Pranava, or Om.
shots.B12C363S116H05: Such a man's eating is said to satisfy the whole universe, with an example of one morsel feeding many pupils.
shots.B12C363S117H01: Such a man regards all things, and himself, as Brahma.
shots.B12C363S117H02: Yasah is read as the great glory, Brahma, and the path of the righteous as Yoga.
shots.B12C363S117H03: Those who perform mental sacrifices are the subject here.
shots.B12C363S117H04: Because the good cannot officiate at others' sacrifices, they act for others' good and avoid all injury.
shots.B12C363S117H05: Only sacrificers who act without desire for fruit reach the end from which there is no return.
shots.B12C363S118H01: They perform mental sacrifices, having created the needed articles by Yoga power rather than offering real ones.
shots.B12C363S118H02: The sin of killing a cow does not touch such a person, since his soul is above the influence of acts.
shots.B12C363S118H03: Renunciation is praised here, not the frame of mind that acts from desire for fruit.
shots.B12C363S118H04: Such a man never bows to another or flatters, since he wants nothing.
shots.B12C363S118H05: The verse says that one who skips these duties misses a desirable end, and the sacrifice is Vishnu or Brahma.
shots.B12C363S119H01: The Munis are mental sacrificers, and the hard Yoga they practise is compared with Tuladhara's.
shots.B12C363S119H02: Yasmin is read as yadi, atmatirtha as the self as holy place, and the singular is used for the plural.
shots.B12C363S119H03: Some lose their sacrifices through lack of faith, while those able to give can perform rites with clarified butter, milk and curds.
shots.B12C363S119H04: The speaker advocates sacrifice without animal slaughter, and the word for sacrifice is taken as Brahma.
shots.B12C363S119H05: The soul is itself a holy place, so merit should be sought within rather than at distant sacred sites.
shots.B12C363S120H01: Dharmasya vachanat kila is read as obeying the voice of Dharma, which is nonviolent.
shots.B12C363S120H02: The two negatives in the second line make an affirmative statement.
shots.B12C363S120H03: Vaivaswati is taken as relating to Brahma, and the daughter of Surya as the Sattwic nature; faith goes beyond speech and mind.
shots.B12C363S120H04: Faults of speech are wrong recitation of mantras, and faults of mind are listlessness and haste.
shots.B12C363S120H05: Kadarya is read as miserly, and vardhushi as a usurer rather than a grain dealer.
shots.B12C363S121H01: The answer focuses on faith: a liberal man's food is sanctified by faith, while a miser's food is not acceptable even with learning.
shots.B12C363S121H02: The commentator reads divam as the power of Yoga rather than ordinary heaven.
shots.B12C363S121H03: Gograhe is a sacrifice in which cows are slain, and the genitive is used for the accusative.
shots.B12C363S121H04: Avyaktaih means those who seek fame through sacrifices.
shots.B12C363S121H05: The slaughter takes place on the outer altar, which the Burdwan translator misreads.
shots.B12C363S122H01: Upasya means living near inhabited places, and the Sannyasa life is recommended over domestic duties.
shots.B12C363S122H02: Ordinary men avoid meat from animals not killed in rites, but the speaker holds all meat tainted, including sacrificial meat.
shots.B12C363S122H03: Sacrifices with animal slaughter and alcohol are therefore unnecessary.
shots.B12C363S122H04: Dangers seek to destroy the body and the body seeks to destroy them, so the speaker asks how anyone can live fully harmless.
shots.B12C363S122H05: One should gain merit without wasting the body, not let it be destroyed for merit.
shots.B12C363S123H01: Rites such as Jata-karma, upakarma and samavartana are described, with the words fathers and teachers speak at them.
shots.B12C363S123H02: Bhogya means goods such as clothes, Bhojya means food, and Simantonnayana is the mark put on the wife's head in pregnancy.
shots.B12C363S123H03: Two sticks once made fire in Indian homes, later replaced by flint and steel, and now by matches.
shots.B12C363S123H04: Prana means the generative organ, and the parents' wishes for a fair, long-lived child depend more on the mother.
shots.B12C363S123H05: Only the mother surely knows the father, so a father's commands may be set aside, and an adulterous father is not to be honoured.
shots.B12C363S124H01: Gautama had stopped protecting his wife, so he had ceased to be her husband and his order to kill her could not be obeyed.
shots.B12C363S124H02: The commentator says that man, being tempted, takes the guilt on himself, while woman, being tempted, escapes it.
shots.B12C363S124H03: The father is all the deities together and the mother all creatures together, so honouring both brings success.
shots.B12C363S124H04: Gautama blames his own carelessness, while the commentator defends Indra by his pure nature, though the note holds Indra to blame.
shots.B12C363S124H05: Prince Satyavat said that the prisoners brought out for execution should not be executed, since kings had no power over subjects' lives.
shots.B12C363S125H02: The Burdwan translator misreads this verse, and K.P. Singha is correct.
shots.B12C363S125H03: The line shows that even a Sannyasin deserves punishment when he offends; K.P. Singha misses this and Burdwan is right.
shots.B12C363S125H04: Both vernacular versions are wrong, and the line about repeated offences applies to offenders in general.
shots.B12C363S125H05: In earlier times punishments were unnecessary or very light, and the Burdwan rendering is absurd.
shots.B12C363S126H01: Extermination is the punishment now judged desirable.
shots.B12C363S126H02: By killing them, no injury is done to anyone in this world or the next.
shots.B12C363S126H03: Padma means the ornaments of corpses, grave-robbers are mentioned, and idiots and madmen are thought possessed by evil spirits.
shots.B12C363S126H04: The prince speaks of slaying wrongdoers as sacrificial beasts, which the Srutis say purges sins, so such death seems milder than hanging.
shots.B12C363S126H05: Conduct improves through a king who behaves properly, so cruel punishments are scarcely needed.
shots.B12C363S127H01: Human life and strength shrink in each succeeding age, so the king should weigh this in awarding punishments.
shots.B12C363S127H02: Satya means liberation, and the true fruit of righteousness is knowledge; verses 32 to 35 seem to be the grandsire's words.
shots.B12C363S127H03: The extra syllable is an arsha usage.
shots.B12C363S127H04: Both acts and knowledge are pointed out in the Vedas, so neither can be blamed or praised.
shots.B12C363S127H05: Arsha means Vedic injunctions revealed to inspired Rishis, and every Vedic word is authoritative.
shots.B12C363S128H01: Deva-yanah is the path by which the Soul is reached, and the four modes of life are ranked by their rewards.
shots.B12C363S128H02: Fearing that doubt about heaven would arise, the speaker justifies slaughter by the need for food, since living creatures must eat.
shots.B12C363S128H03: The essential requisites of sacrifice are mentioned.
shots.B12C363S128H04: Seven domestic animals and seven wild animals are listed.
shots.B12C363S128H05: Vichinwita is read as considering, and atmanah as life.
shots.B12C363S129H01: Not every cow product is needed in every sacrifice; the needed ones, with priests and gifts, complete or sustain it.
shots.B12C363S129H02: Samhritya means gathering into one, not destroying.
shots.B12C363S129H03: The Burdwan translator wrongly joins the first line of verse 31 to verse 30, making both nonsense.
shots.B12C363S129H04: Joining the two lines of verse 32 to the last line of 30 also makes the passage nonsense.
shots.B12C363S129H05: Brahmanas here means the part of the Vedas that contains the ritual.
shots.B12C363S130H01: Each constitutes the refuge of the other.
shots.B12C363S130H02: Words such as hayi and havu are expletives.
shots.B12C363S130H03: One who has gained an empire does not seek charity, and householding yields small rewards next to renunciation.
shots.B12C363S130H04: Grass and grain are cultivated or collected by householders, so domestic life is the root of these.
shots.B12C363S130H05: Vedic mantras enter the twice-born in acts whose effects are seen and unseen, so a Brahmana's acts are done with mantras.
shots.B12C363S131H01: Mantras are needed for cremation, the Sraddha rites and the three debts, so the speaker asks how liberation without a body can fit with them.
shots.B12C363S131H02: Devan means Rishis and Pitris, the amrita is the sacrificial libation, and Brahma-sanjnitah means one who knows Brahma.
shots.B12C363S131H03: The soul has a fourfold nature, its doors are the senses, and Yoga is recommended to control them.
shots.B12C363S131H04: One who has cast off his upper garment dresses scantily only for decency, not for show.
shots.B12C363S131H05: Dwandwarama likely means the joys of married couples, which a Brahmana can enjoy without marrying.
shots.B12C363S132H01: All things are Brahma, their outer forms are transformations, and creatures are reborn until absorbed into Brahma through Yoga.
shots.B12C363S132H02: The terse verse links charity and sacrifice to purity of heart, following the instructions of preceptors, while the other fruit means heaven.
shots.B12C363S132H03: These three verses are abstruse, and the nishkama dharma turns duties into a means of dispelling ignorance.
shots.B12C363S132H04: The Lokayatikas, Buddhists and Kapalikas are the sciences of disputation, along with the two Mimamsas, Sankhya and Patanjala.
shots.B12C363S132H05: Aikatmyam means oneness with everything, which is true knowledge and liberation itself.
shots.B12C363S133H01: Those who rob the scriptures of their meaning and deny God are called robbers and depredators of Brahma.
shots.B12C363S133H02: Anu means following preceptors, and samyame refers to Dharana, Dhyana and Samadhi.
shots.B12C363S133H03: Only renunciation, hard as it is, leads to liberation, and the translators misplace the second line of verse 64.
shots.B12C363S133H04: The Vedas are Sabda-Brahma, Brahma as represented by sound.
shots.B12C363S133H05: The rites from Garbhadhana onward shape the body, and the lesson is that knowledge should follow acts.
shots.B12C363S134H01: Yoga is the only way to true knowledge, so Jnana-nishtha means Yoga-nishtha.
shots.B12C363S134H02: Men like these are pointed out as deserving gifts.
shots.B12C363S134H03: Brahma is meant as possessed of attributes and as free of them.
shots.B12C363S134H04: Matra means understanding, and guile in righteousness is giving barley grains when one could give clothes.
shots.B12C363S134H05: The scriptures often give alternative rules, with the full rule for the able and the alternative for the unable.
shots.B12C363S135H01: Those men were identical with Brahma, had no sense of self, and were the soul of the universe.
shots.B12C363S135H02: At first there was a single course of conduct, sadachara, and later it was divided into four parts matching the four modes of life.
shots.B12C363S135H03: Two translators misunderstand verse 23 and the first line of 24, and the note sets out the construction and the four modes.
shots.B12C363S135H04: The four states of consciousness are waking, dream, dreamless sleep and Turiya, and the common duties lead to Turiya.
shots.B12C363S135H05: Apavargam means knowledge that gives liberation, nityin means necessary, and yatidharma is the life of renunciation.
shots.B12C363S136H01: Sadharana is opposed to kevala, and the one lacking dispassion is the subject; the Burdwan translator misses the sense.
shots.B12C363S136H02: Even if the end reached in the next life is the same, renunciation brings more real happiness than enjoyment.
shots.B12C363S136H03: The Burdwan version of this verse is very wrong.
shots.B12C363S136H05: Vatarechaka is a bellows, and the image suggests a man who breathes in vain.
shots.B12C363S137H01: Nasti refers to past and future, Nishtha is the nature of things, and the Vedas are said to be everything.
shots.B12C363S137H02: The ignorant see the universe as lasting like thunder or adamant, while the man of knowledge sees it as non-existent though it appears to exist.
shots.B12C363S137H03: Renunciation is the complete renunciation reached in Samadhi, and santosha is the supreme bliss of one who has reached Brahma.
shots.B12C363S137H04: The translator follows the commentator on nearly all the adjectives in the verse.
shots.B12C363S137H05: The grammar is hard, and the listed qualities are taken as the cause of a state free of suffering, with the Burdwan version right in sense but wrong in punctuation.
shots.B12C363S138H01: Escape is by expiation, and ingratitude has none because it cannot be expiated.
shots.B12C363S138H02: Asubheshu is read as referring to inauspicious acts that have come up.
shots.B12C363S138H03: The Brahmana is disappointed that Kundadhara did not grant wealth for his worship, so he resolves to give up desire and retire to the forest.
shots.B12C363S138H04: Men of ascetic success speak a wish that is fulfilled at once, so meanings follow their words.
shots.B12C363S138H05: The Burdwan translator misreads etaih as qualifying lokah.
shots.B12C363S139H01: The question asks which sacrifice is meant for duty, and the Burdwan translator misunderstands the commentary.
shots.B12C363S139H02: Unchha means living on grain gleaned from the fields, and the Burdwan rendering wrongly treats it as a name.
shots.B12C363S139H03: Several plants are identified, including a paddy, Suryaparni and Brahmisaka.
shots.B12C363S139H04: The man never killed living animals for sacrifice, substituting vegetable offerings, though his intent was cruel.
shots.B12C363S139H05: Following the Bombay text, the last line of verse 8 refers to a descendant of Sukra, and both vernacular versions are flawed.
shots.B12C363S140H01: K.P. Singha misreads this verse, while the Burdwan translator is right for once.
shots.B12C363S140H02: The commentator reads the verse as fearing other defects in a sacrifice done by an ignorant person.
shots.B12C363S140H03: Vaddhanjalim is an adverb describing ayachata, not an adjective of satyam.
shots.B12C363S140H04: The deer is linked to Parnada in one verse and to Dharma in another, and the notes try to reconcile them.
shots.B12C363S140H05: Yajnia is taken as suited to sacrifice.
shots.B12C363S141H01: Samadhanam is meditative absorption, and bharyayh is genitive rather than instrumental.
shots.B12C363S141H02: The translator reads yo dhamah rather than no dharmah.
shots.B12C363S141H03: The commentator gives the grammar of obtaining one of five things.
shots.B12C363S141H04: Yoga brings a mastery that lets a person create whatever they want by will.
shots.B12C363S141H05: The Burdwan version of this verse is ridiculous.
shots.B12C363S142H01: The man gives up desire-driven duty for duty without desire, the only conduct that leads to liberation.
shots.B12C363S142H02: Dharma here means nishkama dharma, since the fruits of desire-driven duty are not eternal.
shots.B12C363S142H03: As a man stops working once he has his jar, those who gain virtue and seek liberation give up acts for renunciation.
shots.B12C363S142H04: The sense is to give up all kinds of idleness.
shots.B12C363S142H05: Through Yoga one regulates and suspends the breath, and the Yogin can go on living from age to age.
shots.B12C363S143H01: Nidra means lack of inquiry, and pratibha means chasing improper or uninteresting matters.
shots.B12C363S143H02: The world is unreal and has no end.
shots.B12C363S143H03: Hunger is subdued by Yoga breath control, doubt by certain knowledge, and fear by conquering the six passions.
shots.B12C363S143H04: The training merges the senses into the mind, the mind into understanding, understanding into the ego, and the ego into the Supreme Soul.
shots.B12C363S143H05: Pure acts are those of nishkama dharma, and tranquillity is cleansing the soul of passion and desire.
shots.B12C363S144H01: Restraint is yoga, and one should not desire yoga powers, which can lead to hell.
shots.B12C363S144H02: The materials of creation are named, with the Supreme Soul as the unstated creator acting at the chosen time.
shots.B12C363S144H03: Kala is the embodiment of life, which sets creatures in motion through understanding.
shots.B12C363S144H04: All effects belong to the five essences, which are unreal, while the soul alone is real.
shots.B12C363S144H05: When Chit is clouded by ignorance it draws the essences to itself through past acts, and creation proceeds from the essences, Jiva, past acts and ignorance.
shots.B12C363S145H01: Jnanani means the causes of perception.
shots.B12C363S145H02: Sight, its object form and light are linked by attribute, so the eye grasps form.
shots.B12C363S145H03: Manas is mind, buddhi is understanding and kshetrajna is the soul, while chitta is left vague.
shots.B12C363S145H04: The Bengal reading yathagantam is preferred to the Bombay reading.
shots.B12C363S145H05: In dreamless sleep, waking and dream notions merge and become directly known, which is emancipation.
shots.B12C363S146H02: Brahmabhava means understanding Brahma, and the learned see the soul's attainment through scripture.
shots.B12C363S146H03: Men of knowledge do not value even the joy of the creator's region.
shots.B12C363S146H04: One should not want wealth even for virtue, and wealth that comes without effort should go to virtue, since desire grows.
shots.B12C363S146H05: The man of knowledge should wish happiness for all and sorrow for none, practising nishkama dharma.
shots.B12C363S147H01: Brahmanas pluck flowers each morning for worship, often with the mind elsewhere.
shots.B12C363S147H02: The Bengal reading is preferred for the tiger image, which seems unfamiliar in the Bombay form.
shots.B12C363S147H03: The senses are like cattle, and their true fold is the forest, which has fewer temptations than towns.
shots.B12C363S147H04: Jivitarthapanayenaih goes with hinsati, not with pranibhih.
shots.B12C363S147H05: Sacrifices of peace, Brahma, speech, mind and acts are described, with Yoga, recitation, contemplation and purity as their forms.
shots.B12C363S148H01: The sacrifice of self is merging the soul in the Supreme Soul.
shots.B12C363S148H02: The Bombay danda-vidhanam is an error for danda nidhanam, and vidhanam should not be read as giving up.
shots.B12C363S148H03: The guha or cave is the body.
shots.B12C363S148H04: Prakriti means primal nature made of the five great essences.
shots.B12C363S148H05: Samupodeshu means even when such objects are present and ready for enjoyment.
shots.B12C363S149H01: The seeker should roam like the sun on separate paths and never settle in one spot.
shots.B12C363S149H02: The Bengal reading madhya na chacharet is preferred, and the mendicant begs from many houses.
shots.B12C363S149H03: The muni begs at an hour when the house has least to give, and patrasamchara means the movements of those serving food.
shots.B12C363S149H04: Matra means eating only enough to satisfy hunger, which is all the mendicant takes.
shots.B12C363S149H05: When honoured, such a man should regard it with reproach, as the Sanatsujatiya sections say.
shots.B12C363S150H01: The second line is passed over, and the Brahmana's practices are meant to be hidden.
shots.B12C363S150H02: By abstaining from acts entirely, a man avoids both merit and demerit.
shots.B12C363S150H03: This is a triplet, and bhutanam means the other beings.
shots.B12C363S150H04: Thinking ahead about food turns a man into a gourmand, so he takes what comes without effort.
shots.B12C363S150H05: Sanjnakam is derived from a root meaning death or killing.
shots.B12C363S151H01: Affluence, through the attachment it breeds, blocks liberation, and the king's view on it is correct.
shots.B12C363S151H02: The verse urges Yudhishthira to strive for liberation regardless of happiness and misery.
shots.B12C363S151H03: Like the colourless wind taking on colours, Jiva takes stains from ignorance and acts, though its source is stainless.
shots.B12C363S151H04: Acts are terminable so cannot reach Brahma, knowledge dispels ignorance, and reverence for those who have attained Brahma matters.
shots.B12C363S151H05: Intermediate beings are animals, birds, reptiles and worms.
shots.B12C363S152H01: The righteous attain happiness and the unrighteous the reverse.
shots.B12C363S152H02: Verse 21 and the first line of verse 22 are grammatically linked.
shots.B12C363S152H03: Hari, who came to aid Indra, is named for taking away sins, and Narayana is derived as a resting place of beings.
shots.B12C363S152H04: The commentator lists epithets of Vishnu, including Vaikuntha, Purusha, Sanatana and Munjakesa.
shots.B12C363S152H05: The speaker says the sight of Hari was as good as the severest penance, and asking about acts is itself a reward.
shots.B12C363S153H01: Outer acts are sacrifices and inner acts are the mental training for Yoga, and sacrifices can cleanse the heart.
shots.B12C363S153H02: The comparison lies in the desire to remove stains from body and heart, not in the effort each needs.
shots.B12C363S153H03: Efforts born of practice cover both external and internal discipline.
shots.B12C363S153H04: Karmaviseshan is explained as the cause of attachment and aversion.
shots.B12C363S153H05: The verbs sampravartante and tishthanti are explained as the commentator does.
shots.B12C363S154H01: The names Sreeman, Hari, Narayana, Prabhu and Deva are etymologised, and must be grasped to follow the verse.
shots.B12C363S154H02: The mutable is the five essences, the immutable is Jiva, and the eleven senses are the rays through which the universe is enjoyed.
shots.B12C363S154H03: The mind is the moon, and the Ganges image shows no gap between container and contained.
shots.B12C363S154H04: The sandhi between sa and acramanam is arsha.
shots.B12C363S154H05: Dharma has many meanings, and as duty it is both righteousness and religion.
shots.B12C363S155H01: The sacrificial vessels are named for deities such as Indra, Vayu and Soma, and the sixteen priests include Brahman and Hotri.
shots.B12C363S155H02: Verses 21 to 23 show the unity of the Divine, with variety being only apparent.
shots.B12C363S155H03: The Burdwan translator makes nonsense of verses 31 and 32, which are plain.
shots.B12C363S155H04: The Vishnu Purana links six colours to creations, from the dark for immobile beings to the white for the Kumaras.
shots.B12C363S155H05: Emancipation is very hard to reach.
shots.B12C363S156H01: The grammar of the first line is set out, with gati depending on varna and varna on time or acts.
shots.B12C363S156H02: Ten senses and four inner faculties make fourteen, and Jiva moves up and down the scale, so these should be kept towards sattwa.
shots.B12C363S156H03: This life turns Jiva into an immobile object, and the dark-hued who turn to wicked acts end in hell.
shots.B12C363S156H04: Prajavisarga is the span of one creation, equal to a kalpa.
shots.B12C363S156H05: The dark and tawny states are regarded as periods of endurance, after which the memory of old righteousness returns.
shots.B12C363S157H01: After the tawny state, Jiva reaches humanity when sattwa is not dominant.
shots.B12C363S157H02: The verb is a finite indicative, and the Burdwan rendering is self-contradictory.
shots.B12C363S157H03: A deva still has nineteen faculties driving thousands of acts, so he is not free of acts.
shots.B12C363S157H04: The seven faculties, acted out a hundredfold, carry Jiva through red, yellow and white, and white beings reach regions above Brahma's.
shots.B12C363S157H05: The verse's sixty states run from waking and the gross body through the faculties, and the total is doubled by dream.
shots.B12C363S158H01: A Jivanmukta who cannot shed yoga's felicities stays for a century of kalpas in a higher form, then passes through four regions.
shots.B12C363S158H02: The yogin who falls from yoga dwells in heaven for a century of kalpas, then returns to earth with his eminence kept.
shots.B12C363S158H03: A yogin who reaches only the first stage ascends to heaven, then returns as an emperor, and climbs higher with each step.
shots.B12C363S158H04: The seven regions are the worlds or the senses with mind and understanding, and the sects name the highest region in different ways.
shots.B12C363S158H05: The verse is not difficult, yet the Burdwan version is nonsense and K.P. Singha skips the second line.
shots.B12C363S159H01: For one who knows Brahma the whole universe is as close as a plum in the palm, once the Chitta is cleansed by Yoga.
shots.B12C363S159H02: Two stages are named: attaining the stainless end, which is Brahma-realisation, and the unchanging spot of emancipation.
shots.B12C363S159H03: The commentator says God is impersonal at the root of all, and Bhagavan is the same God endowed with powers through Avidya.
shots.B12C363S159H04: God is in the form of all things, causes and effects.
shots.B12C363S159H05: Vritra was a firm devotee of Vishnu, so the commentator asks how Indra could defeat him.
shots.B12C363S160H01: Vinihatah and nirjitah both mean the same thing.
shots.B12C363S160H03: Rathantara is a Saman name, meaning a means of crossing the world like a chariot.
shots.B12C363S160H04: The Rishis sing hymns praising Indra's victory.
shots.B12C363S160H05: Raudrah may also mean belonging to Rudra, another name for Mahadeva.
shots.B12C363S161H01: This account of Vritra and Indra differs from the Vana Parva, and the Rishis' part in the killing is censurable.
shots.B12C363S161H02: Amanusham, literally inhuman, is a slip of the poet, as Homer also nods.
shots.B12C363S161H03: Vadhya is slaughter in embodied form.
shots.B12C363S161H04: Vritra was a descendant of Kasyapa and a superior being, so killing him was the slaughter of a noble Brahmana.
shots.B12C363S161H05: The rule referred to concerns the slayer of a Brahmana being overtaken by the sin of Brahmanicide.
shots.B12C363S162H02: Uma is Parvati, daughter of Himavat and wife of Siva.
shots.B12C363S162H03: Brahman created the Prajapatis, including Daksha, though other accounts make Daksha his grandson.
shots.B12C363S162H04: Three vocatives express surprise, and the translation omits them.
shots.B12C363S162H05: Silajit is a substance that oozes from mountain stones in hot months and is taken for digestion and strength.
shots.B12C363S163H01: The Indian cuckoo is a favourite bird of the poets.
shots.B12C363S163H02: The line means that Uma, unlike Siva, should already know him, and K.P. Singha skips it.
shots.B12C363S163H03: Both translators err: Mahadeva says Uma is the one who stupefies others, and it surprises him to see her stupefied.
shots.B12C363S163H04: Mahadeva is called Virupaksha and Tryaksha for his three eyes.
shots.B12C363S163H05: Worshippers of Mahadeva strike their cheeks with air-filled mouths, making a booming sound that he enjoys.
shots.B12C363S164H01: Vrisha, Vrishya, Go-vrisha, Katankata and Danda are explained as titles of Siva.
shots.B12C363S164H02: Godhead is compared to unheard sound in its nascent state.
shots.B12C363S164H03: Huns are mystic sounds, and beyond three huns may mean beyond anger.
shots.B12C363S164H04: Butter is poured into a Brahmana who represents the gods and into the fire, so the great god is in that Brahmana and the fire.
shots.B12C363S164H05: The line alludes to Krishna's play in the Vrinda groves with his rustic companions.
shots.B12C363S165H01: The Ganges falls on Siva's head, and of the six Brahmana acts Siva performs sacrifice, study and giving.
shots.B12C363S165H02: Sankhya means the sceptical philosophy, Sankhya-mukhya is the foremost follower of Patanjala, and Sankhya-yoga covers Vedanta and Yoga.
shots.B12C363S165H03: Having a car and having no car means moving freely through water, fire, wind and space.
shots.B12C363S165H04: Isana means much desired by all.
shots.B12C363S165H05: The line means you create and destroy these repeatedly, or set them in motion.
shots.B12C363S166H01: The filler syllables are sung by Saman chanters to lengthen short words and keep the metre.
shots.B12C363S166H02: The one adored in these hymns is the god himself and no other.
shots.B12C363S166H03: These are the ten colours known to the Rishis.
shots.B12C363S166H04: Red eyes means lotus-coloured eyes, and inward eyes means one absorbed in samadhi.
shots.B12C363S166H05: Chalachalah means exceedingly swift, so the unmoving one is swifter than the swiftest.
shots.B12C363S167H01: The great god is a fish wandering in the waters and caught in the net, as Jiva wanders and is held by darkness.
shots.B12C363S167H02: Meghakala and the clouds Samvartaka and Valahaka mark the time of universal deluge.
shots.B12C363S167H03: Mili is read as cause of causes, and the staff-bearing bald man is a paramahansa who has renounced the world.
shots.B12C363S167H04: The four sacrificial fires are named.
shots.B12C363S167H05: Silpika means one unskilled in the arts, a common artisan.
shots.B12C363S168H01: Dhatri is read as Vishnu, and Vidhatri as the four-headed Brahman, who joins all things and designs destinies.
shots.B12C363S168H02: The identity of Mahesvara with Narayana is preached, and Krishna sported with the cowherd children and guarded their kine.
shots.B12C363S168H03: The word Go in Gomargah stands for the senses.
shots.B12C363S168H04: Durvaranah means irresistible as Death, durvishah destroyer of poison, and durdharshah one who cannot be frightened.
shots.B12C363S168H05: Vishagnipah means drinker of poison and fire, a sign that Siva accepts what others reject, as when he swallowed the churned poison.
shots.B12C363S169H01: The correct reading is tushitadyapah, and the protected one is Brahman himself.
shots.B12C363S169H02: Mahadeva being alone means he is knower, known and knowledge, and beyond desire and attachment.
shots.B12C363S169H03: Yogins are the subject of the verse.
shots.B12C363S169H04: Eclipses come from Rahu, an Asura whose head alone survives, and who swallows the sun and moon.
shots.B12C363S169H05: The deities are called embryos born in Mahadeva, and anu means after Brahman's creation.
shots.B12C363S170H01: These beings are parts of the great Rudra.
shots.B12C363S170H02: Param means the superior practices such as renunciation, offered to Iswara.
shots.B12C363S170H03: Every Kalpa must resemble the one before, so the speaker must do the same in this one.
shots.B12C363S170H04: Matri-paksha seems a misreading for bhartri-paksha.
shots.B12C363S170H05: Guna means all that makes up the body, mind and understanding, which accompany the soul.
shots.B12C363S171H01: Karma-buddhi is each sense's grasp of its own function, and the mind completes the tale of six.
shots.B12C363S171H02: Acts means the desires of past lives in an incipient form.
shots.B12C363S171H03: Buddhya is read as an instrumental, with kalpitani understood.
shots.B12C363S171H04: The senses occupy their objects one after another.
shots.B12C363S171H05: Murti is a misreading for apurti, discontentedness, and the Bengali substitute suggests stupefaction.
shots.B12C363S172H01: Sattwa or buddhi has no material basis or cause.
shots.B12C363S172H02: Verses 41 and 42 argue that the qualities of the body persist in the subtle body, and rebirth shows it.
shots.B12C363S172H03: The second line reads as ignorant of its depth, and agadham is masculine and cannot qualify the feminine nadi.
shots.B12C363S172H04: The man of knowledge destroys sins of this life and past lives, like a lotus leaf unwetted by water, and does not censure others.
shots.B12C363S172H05: Even in direst distress one depends only on oneself, crossing life's river with bare arms.
shots.B12C363S173H01: What does not exist and will not exist is non-existent, and sorrow is bound up with what is not real.
shots.B12C363S173H02: Acts bring sorrow, their fruits vary, and the man who avoids acts grieves neither for lack nor for unwanted gain.
shots.B12C363S173H03: Those who avoid acts still live as others do, though their circumstances differ.
shots.B12C363S173H04: Ignorance is the root of sorrow, so religious acts can neither help nor harm, and happiness and misery are fleeting.
shots.B12C363S173H05: No one should boast of happiness or yield to misery, since both pass.
shots.B12C363S174H01: The opening word has two readings, one meaning worldly form and the other visible form.
shots.B12C363S174H02: The speaker must look on the world as an unconcerned witness, since he is embodied.
shots.B12C363S174H03: The scriptures give both kinds of instruction, and the speaker asks which path to follow.
shots.B12C363S174H04: Each asrama praises its own observances, which confuses plain minds, so the question is whether duties differ in value.
shots.B12C363S174H05: Asrama is kept as a word, and the commentator reads it as four principal creeds, from the denial of virtue to the view that virtue is what the Vedas lay down.
shots.B12C363S175H01: Gunoddesam means the announcement of merits, and each asrama claims its merit leads to self-knowledge, though the claims conflict.
shots.B12C363S175H02: Te refers to the asramas, and abhipretam is the nature of the soul.
shots.B12C363S175H03: Mitra means those who have pledged harmlessness to all, and enemies are the envious and harmful.
shots.B12C363S175H04: A formal truth may be as sinful as a lie, and a lie may be meritorious, so truth is hard to ascertain.
shots.B12C363S175H05: Atiyoga and ayoga are plain words that both translators misread.
shots.B12C363S176H01: The phrase means a mixing of the four orders, varna-sankara.
shots.B12C363S176H02: Company of the righteous leads to righteous acts, and company of the sinful to sinful ones.
shots.B12C363S176H03: Anuvishayam means flavour, and a vighasa eater is a good man who eats only to fill his stomach.
shots.B12C363S176H04: Agamayamanam is knowledge from scripture that the self desires.
shots.B12C363S176H05: Akasasthah means those with no foundation, and the singular form is taken as qualifying panditah.
shots.B12C363S177H01: Desires born of past lives cling to the mind, and only Nivritti and knowledge of truth can wipe them off.
shots.B12C363S177H02: Both translators skip the word pratyanantarah.
shots.B12C363S177H03: The place referred to is one where people are virtuous and do their duties.
shots.B12C363S177H04: Kamesah means possessor of desired objects, so the king is wealthy without being attached to wealth.
shots.B12C363S177H05: Pratyupasthite is read as having come near with goodwill.
shots.B12C363S178H01: The translator is unsure of the second line, which may mean no one can list all that benefits the soul.
shots.B12C363S178H02: Vrittam is read with uddisya understood, and the Bengal pranihitatmanah means a soul fixed in yoga.
shots.B12C363S178H03: Sampadam is the splendour of being fit for instruction.
shots.B12C363S178H04: Some texts read sakyam, and neither reading changes the sense.
shots.B12C363S178H05: The correct reading is lokeshu, not lobheshu, and both translators follow the wrong one.
shots.B12C363S179H01: Mokshartha means having liberation as its aim.
shots.B12C363S179H02: Since one cannot help dying relatives, one should not neglect one's own liberation by caring for them.
shots.B12C363S179H03: One who takes only a handful of corn, though carts of grain await, is freed and sees no difference between palace and shed.
shots.B12C363S179H04: Avritti means lack of the means to live, hence scarcity or famine.
shots.B12C363S179H05: Supporting wives and children is painful, so one should withdraw into solitude.
shots.B12C363S180H01: Domestic life is allowed if one behaves as described, and Sannyasa in solitude is the way to liberation.
shots.B12C363S180H02: The planet Venus is taken to be the sage Usanas or Sukra.
shots.B12C363S180H03: Vishnu, urged by the gods, struck off the head of Usanas' mother with his discus, so Usanas turned against the gods and aided their foes.
shots.B12C363S180H04: The construction is very hard; Indra is the lord of the world, and Dhanada's treasury is under his power.
shots.B12C363S180H05: Those crowned with yoga-success can enter other bodies and take away their will.
shots.B12C363S181H01: Pinaka is derived from parts of pani and anamayat with the suffix ka.
shots.B12C363S181H02: The last half of the last line may be taken as applying to Usanas.
shots.B12C363S181H03: The greatness Mahadeva saw cannot be his own, so it is Usanas' greatness inside Mahadeva's stomach.
shots.B12C363S181H04: The word sa refers to Usanas and not to Mahadeva.
shots.B12C363S181H05: The phrase means the religions of all orders and all modes of life.
shots.B12C363S182H01: The injunctions to worship the gods, pour libations and make gifts are where righteousness lies.
shots.B12C363S182H02: The third line is grammatically involved, and people of every mode believe in righteousness and perform their duties.
shots.B12C363S182H03: The sinful become intermediate animals, the virtuous reach heaven, the mixed become human, and those with knowledge are liberated.
shots.B12C363S182H04: Destiny means the results of past acts.
shots.B12C363S182H05: Reading jatikritam karma makes this the sceptic's argument, and the four kinds of acts are named.
shots.B12C363S183H01: Verses 12 to 14 give the sceptic's view, and verse 15 is the speaker's own answer, which dismisses the sceptic.
shots.B12C363S183H02: Nature as the cause is answered: fire is hot by nature, yet states differ because causes differ.
shots.B12C363S183H03: A Brahmana must keep food rules, and one who takes cooked food without sharing it with the yati and brahmachari eats what belongs to a Brahmana.
shots.B12C363S183H04: Seva is devotion and meditation on the Supreme with full reliance on God, learned from a competent preceptor.
shots.B12C363S183H05: The verse urges that seva be practised soon, without loss of time.
shots.B12C363S184H01: The six colours appear in Sanatkumara's discourse to Vritra, with the acts that raise or lower one's colour.
shots.B12C363S184H02: A particular kind of Chandala is called kusalin.
shots.B12C363S184H03: Pratyapanna means reversed perception, and virochate means shines as the self.
shots.B12C363S184H04: Pratyapatti means renunciation, and prasthita may mean the dead or one who has taken to yoga.
shots.B12C363S184H05: Conscious sin can never be destroyed by expiation; only enduring its fruit removes it.
shots.B12C363S185H01: The Burdwan translator makes nonsense of this verse; guna-yuktam means virtuous deeds, and prakasam means done knowingly.
shots.B12C363S185H02: Acts done knowingly yield fruits in kind, gross for gross and subtle for subtle.
shots.B12C363S185H03: Acts done in ignorance yield smaller fruits of misery, even when heinous.
shots.B12C363S185H04: Such acts are set aside in this discourse, since Viswamitra killed Vasishtha's hundred sons yet avoided hell.
shots.B12C363S185H05: Relatives who lack affection are cast off, since people do good to others only when they gain by it.
shots.B12C363S186H01: Accepting a gift from a superior person equals a poor man's gift in merit, while a rich man earns more by giving than by receiving.
shots.B12C363S186H03: The verse refers to Usanas taking his place as a planet in the sky.
shots.B12C363S186H04: Nadantah is one word meaning free from injury, and the commentator derives danta from cutting.
shots.B12C363S187H01: People take on the hue of their company, so it is wise to keep the good.
shots.B12C363S187H02: The son of Dhatri is the god of the clouds.
shots.B12C363S187H03: The Burdwan translator wrongly makes Dhigdanda a king's name, while K.P. Singha has the right sense.
shots.B12C363S187H04: The enjoyment of objects is carried to excess, and Devan and Brahman are objects of Avamanya.
shots.B12C363S187H05: The three Asuras are Kama, Krodha and Lobha, read metaphorically as the spiritual destruction of evil passions.
shots.B12C363S188H01: The chief Asura passion is great heedlessness, and the Devas here may mean the senses.
shots.B12C363S188H02: Adhering to acts and making them a precedent is hard to render literally.
shots.B12C363S188H03: Samsiddhadhigamam means attaining the eternal self, which is self-knowledge.
shots.B12C363S188H04: The gods too are subject to fortune and misfortune, love and hate, as are all modes of life.
shots.B12C363S188H05: A verb is understood after sukham, and tyajatam refers to optional acts.
shots.B12C363S189H01: Many take up penance out of despair, but few do so because they see domestic happiness as unreal and ending in misery.
shots.B12C363S189H02: These are the penances of past lives.
shots.B12C363S189H03: Akrita-karmanam is explained as those who have not gained knowledge, and renunciation is giving up enjoyments.
shots.B12C363S189H04: The second line concludes the argument, referring back to all the earlier statements.
shots.B12C363S189H05: The second line is expanded for clarity.
shots.B12C363S190H01: Stainless penances means penances done without desire for fruit.
shots.B12C363S190H02: Penance without desire brings happiness, while penance with desire brings many sorrows from the wealth it wins.
shots.B12C363S190H03: The first line only makes sense if vidhitsa is not joined to dharma and the others.
shots.B12C363S190H04: Tatah means because of the pain that follows sense-pleasure, and the highest fruit is liberation.
shots.B12C363S190H05: Destiny governs spouses and food, while exertion can gain righteousness, and the scriptures would be meaningless without that distinction.
shots.B12C363S191H01: Sacrifices done from vanity are destructible, since heaven ends, while penances without desire lead to liberation.
shots.B12C363S191H02: Kam is Brahman; the commentator makes a Sudra who keeps all duties a Brahmana next life, though Parasara says he becomes a Kshatriya.
shots.B12C363S191H03: The translator is unsure of verses 32 and 33 and calls verse 33 a crux.
shots.B12C363S191H04: Yathakarman means from one stage to another, and the stages are vichara, vitarka, Ananda and Asmita.
shots.B12C363S191H05: The Burdwan translator misrenders the second line, which all texts read the same way.
shots.B12C363S192H01: Mothers rubbing oil on ill children is forbidden, since elders should not perform menial offices.
shots.B12C363S192H02: Vinasamabhikankhatam has an alternative reading, explained as observant of the duties of tirtha-dwellers.
shots.B12C363S192H03: The commentator explains the second line in the plain, exoteric sense.
shots.B12C363S192H04: One who dies suddenly in a tirtha takes another body like the one lost, and though set on the path, remains a traveller because of his inglorious end.
shots.B12C363S192H05: The man who dies in a sacred place becomes a Rudra or a Pisacha and reaches liberation through nearness to Siva.
shots.B12C363S193H01: The objects of the senses exist only as they exist in desire, shaped by the desires of past lives.
shots.B12C363S193H02: All acts are perishable in their consequences.
shots.B12C363S193H03: Apamrityu means ignominious accidental death, such as from a snakebite, a fall, drowning or an animal's horn.
shots.B12C363S193H04: Both yasya and sa refer to ignorance, and rajaputra is a vocative meaning the prince.
shots.B12C363S193H05: Vanchate is preceded by kamena understood.
shots.B12C363S194H01: Sreyas or nisreyas means good or excellent as applied to moral merit.
shots.B12C363S194H02: Buddhiman is the man freed from attachment, and durbuddhih the slave of attachments.
shots.B12C363S194H03: Sin can never be destroyed except by enduring its fruits.
shots.B12C363S194H04: Like a magnet, Jiva draws the status of Brahma to itself through yoga.
shots.B12C363S194H05: Sesame seeds grow fragrant when mixed with oil, and men gain sattwa by association with pure souls, in measure to the association.
shots.B12C363S195H01: The track is that of knowledge.
shots.B12C363S195H02: Diverse means the fruits of unstable enjoyment through varied acts, and few means renunciation, and both vernacular versions are wrong.
shots.B12C363S195H03: The lotus-stalk simile is unclear, since the stalk's roots lie in mire.
shots.B12C363S195H04: The universe created by the mind is destroyed afterwards by the mind itself.
shots.B12C363S195H05: One who has cast off objects of enjoyment and become liberated is not reborn.
shots.B12C363S196H01: Fishermen sink their boats when they go home and raise them the next day, and the verse is read with this practice.
shots.B12C363S196H02: Prakriti is the balance of sattwa, rajas and tamas, and while they stay balanced there is no creation or working of the understanding.
shots.B12C363S196H04: One who takes the body for the soul, and thinks inner purity alone can cleanse him without bathing at sacred waters, is the subject.
shots.B12C363S196H05: This refers back to a note on verse 21 above.
shots.B12C363S197H01: One should not give up the true end for friends, kin, spouse or children, and charity is the real food that sustains a man.
shots.B12C363S197H02: Astapadapada is a measure of gold, and mother and others are like lines traced beside real gold, of no use for gaining wealth; the Burdwan rendering is nonsense and daksha is a vocative.
shots.B12C363S197H03: Apariharavan means that which cannot be resisted, and the bond is made with iron or a saw.
shots.B12C363S197H04: Tapah is one's own duties, damah is restraint of the senses, satyam is truthful speech, and the knots are attachments and desires.
shots.B12C363S197H05: A victim who forgives leaves the attacker burning with repentance.
shots.B12C363S198H01: The reading vishayena yami is correct, with vishayena in the instrumental case.
shots.B12C363S198H02: The Moon waxes and wanes and the wind moves fast or slow, so neither equals a man who stays the same through all changes.
shots.B12C363S198H03: The verse shows the merits of one whose ignorance has disappeared.
shots.B12C363S198H04: Brahmanas who suffer obloquy are called impure, and they count as human only because they die.
shots.B12C363S198H05: Viswamitra and others can be cited as examples.
shots.B12C363S199H01: Dharana is holding the soul in self-reflection, and samadhi is complete abstraction.
shots.B12C363S199H02: Akhandam means always, and the translator wrongly takes mansam for masam.
shots.B12C363S199H03: The commentator lists ten qualities of sattwa, nine of rajas, eight of tamas, and the incidents of buddhi, mind and the elements, with other schools giving other counts.
shots.B12C363S199H04: Durga is an inaccessible region, a forest or wilderness hard to cross.
shots.B12C363S200H01: Udadhi is a water-jar, used by swimmers as a buoy, and milkmaids are said to cross swift currents this way.
shots.B12C363S200H02: The second line of verse 72 reads dustaram janma as janma-yuktam dustaram.
shots.B12C363S200H03: Sankhya practice makes men regard their bodies as nothing, and their power is one of knowledge rather than yoga, so even Indra's and Brahman's positions seem unworthy.
shots.B12C363S200H04: The Sankhyas are said to be taken to the sky of the heart, withdrawn from external impressions.
shots.B12C363S200H05: The phrase may mean the pleasures of heaven.
shots.B12C363S201H01: Those who identify themselves with Brahma are meant.
shots.B12C363S201H02: Yudhishthira asks whether consciousness exists in the liberated state, and the answer decides whether acts or renunciation is better; dnkshataram is glossed as ayuktaram.
shots.B12C363S201H03: The word perceive also covers recollection and representation, since the mind counts as the sixth sense, and the Burdwan rendering is badly wrong.
shots.B12C363S201H04: The froth simile is used for its vanishing with the water, and K.P. Singha misreads it as showing speed.
shots.B12C363S201H05: Sarvatra means in every object of the senses, not in every part of the sleeper's body.
shots.B12C363S202H01: Iha means in the dream, and anisah means one with no lord or guiding power.
shots.B12C363S202H02: In dreams the soul sees, hears, touches and smells just as it does awake.
shots.B12C363S202H03: One emancipated in samadhi returns to mind and senses when it ends and meets the fruits of past acts without feeling them.
shots.B12C363S202H04: There are two kinds of liberation, Jivan-mukti in this body and Videha-kaivalya without a body, and this verse concerns the latter.
shots.B12C363S202H05: Vadanti means they praise it, and the attributes ascribed to Brahma come from illusion.
shots.B12C363S203H01: Brahma is knowledge without duality, with no split between knower and known.
shots.B12C363S203H02: Among moving beings those with knowledge are higher, and Sankhya knowledge is the highest of all.
shots.B12C363S203H03: Even if Sankhyas fall short of liberation, they are made into gods.
shots.B12C363S203H05: Narayana, who does all this, is the embodiment of the Sankhya system.
shots.B12C363S204H01: The commentator reads the compound adhyatmagatinischayam differently.
shots.B12C363S204H02: Both vernacular translators render this verse wrongly.
shots.B12C363S204H03: Vasyante is taken as the end of Brahman's day and night, and Vasishtha here means the great dissolution.
shots.B12C363S204H04: In the creation of Mahan, Prajapati, Virat and consciousness, the element of Tamas predominates.
shots.B12C363S204H05: The verse describes how Hiranyagarbha and Virat came from Akshara, and how attributing and withdrawing attributes arose before men were there.
shots.B12C363S205H01: From Akshara comes Hiranyagarbha, from which come Mahan or Virat and consciousness, and from them the subtle elements.
shots.B12C363S205H02: Prakriti is the ruler of the universe, while Vishnu or the Indestructible pervades it without ruling.
shots.B12C363S205H03: Tamas brings birth among the lower orders, Rajas among men and Sattwa among gods, and the root kshi means power.
shots.B12C363S205H04: The soul weaves a cocoon out of attributes, and though free it deprives itself of freedom.
shots.B12C363S205H05: The phrase means made of both Chit and not-Chit.
shots.B12C363S206H01: Explaining a treatise before a learned gathering sharpens the best faculties and brings out the right sense.
shots.B12C363S206H03: Pranayama with mantras is called saguna, while concentration made without them is not.
shots.B12C363S206H04: The twenty-two channels carry prana from the toe to the crown, and what transcends Prakriti is the Supreme Soul.
shots.B12C363S207H01: The soul is higher than Iswara.
shots.B12C363S207H02: Parisankhyadarsanam means the gradual dispelling of error and direct vision.
shots.B12C363S207H03: Nistattwah is explained as one from whom the directly perceived truth has departed.
shots.B12C363S207H04: Param and aparam belong to the imperishable, with aparam as the power of desires coming true and param as the joy of samadhi.
shots.B12C363S207H05: Knowing the Unmanifest makes one capable of omniscience.
shots.B12C363S208H01: Prakriti produces Mahat and the rest only with Purusha's agency, so each depends on the other and both can be called Kshara.
shots.B12C363S208H02: The term refers to Jiva or Purusha.
shots.B12C363S208H03: High beings are gods, middling ones are humans, and low ones are animals.
shots.B12C363S208H04: Budha means pure knowledge and abudha its reverse; the Supreme Soul is knowledge and Jiva is ignorance.
shots.B12C363S208H05: Joined to Prakriti, Jiva takes objects for a vessel or a mountain, and once knowledge comes it sees the world as a modification of the Self.
shots.B12C363S209H01: Drisya and adrisya mean the seen and the unseen, gross and subtle, and Brahma pervades all things without changing its nature.
shots.B12C363S209H02: Tattwa is invested with form through ignorance, and not-tattwa is always within the ken of understanding.
shots.B12C363S209H03: That indication is I am Brahma, a conviction even the awakened set aside at the twenty-sixth.
shots.B12C363S209H04: The gnat in the ripe fig and the fish in water show that Jiva lives in the Supreme Soul without being it.
shots.B12C363S209H05: Para is the other, the pure Chit, and paradharma means partaking of the nature of the field where it dwells.
shots.B12C363S210H01: Honey gatherers who followed bees over mountains often fell from precipices, a simile for chasing sense-objects.
shots.B12C363S210H02: The Burdwan translator renders this verse incorrectly.
shots.B12C363S210H03: Gifts give no merit unless made to the deserving, and time and place matter, so truth can be sinful and falsehood meritorious.
shots.B12C363S210H04: With mind included, these make up the sixteen modifications of Prakriti.
shots.B12C363S210H05: These are the subtle principles, not the gross elements.
shots.B12C363S211H01: Mahat is sometimes called Buddhi, so the creation of consciousness from Mahat relates to Buddha.
shots.B12C363S211H02: Arjjava means relating to straight courses, named for the straight paths of these winds.
shots.B12C363S211H03: Rishi here means Mahan, and consciousness is a bhuta able to produce the five great bhutas.
shots.B12C363S211H04: The commentator names these as mind, buddhi, consciousness and chitta.
shots.B12C363S211H05: Consciousness and chitta are taken as individual rather than collective.
shots.B12C363S212H01: The Prajapatis are the sires of the primeval sires, from whom the great elements sprang.
shots.B12C363S212H02: The Mahabhutas are the great creatures, the five primal elements.
shots.B12C363S212H03: The commentator reads Devas as the senses and four inner faculties and Devaih as the elements, and his view should not be rejected.
shots.B12C363S212H04: The two verses show how the attributes of sound and the rest bind Jiva, with loves and hates arising from them.
shots.B12C363S212H05: The duration given is the day and night of the Mahabhutas.
shots.B12C363S213H01: Purusha, though in the body Prakriti provides, is not defiled by Prakriti.
shots.B12C363S213H02: The translator expands the verse, since a word-for-word rendering would be unintelligible.
shots.B12C363S213H03: Prakriti is unintelligent, yet feels pleasure and pain through union with the intelligent Purusha.
shots.B12C363S213H04: The first line of verse 7 and the second of verse 8 have the same sense, and Tattwa and Prakriti are one.
shots.B12C363S213H05: This refers to the atheistic Sankhyas.
shots.B12C363S214H01: Rudra means the vital breaths, and yogins who regulate breath and senses can roam in subtle bodies.
shots.B12C363S214H02: The eight limbs of yoga are named, with yama and niyama added.
shots.B12C363S214H03: Pranayama means control of the breath in the first line and of the senses in the second, and dharana fixes the mind on sixteen things.
shots.B12C363S214H04: Saguna pranayama measures inhaling, holding and exhaling by mentally reciting a mantra, and these are puraka, kumbhaka and rechaka.
shots.B12C363S214H05: Ekantasilin means a sannyasin, and atmarama one who delights in his own soul.
shots.B12C363S215H02: Chakre literally means I made, and it is explained as having appeared of itself.
shots.B12C363S215H03: The vipriya dispute between Yajnavalkya and his uncle Vaisampayana was over fees at Janaka's sacrifice, and the Vishnu Purana tells of the Vedas being vomited forth and taken by birds.
shots.B12C363S215H04: The speaker was counted equal to Vaisampayana in Vedic knowledge, and Sumanta, Paila and Jaimini helped Vyasa arrange the Vedas.
shots.B12C363S215H05: A fourth science is named alongside the three Vedas and the sciences of worldly affairs and of punishment.
shots.B12C363S216H01: Prakriti has the three qualities in exactly equal measure, and the principles derived from it have them in varying measure.
shots.B12C363S216H02: Mitra is the giver of light and heat, and Varuna is the waters that make up the universe.
shots.B12C363S216H03: The commentator explains kah as felicity.
shots.B12C363S216H04: Trying to learn Prakriti and Purusha from the Vedas without understanding is like churning ass's milk for butter.
shots.B12C363S216H05: The other Soul is the real Soul apart from its reflection in Prakriti; it sees Prakriti in waking and dream and the Supreme in samadhi.
shots.B12C363S217H01: The Supreme Soul always sees the Jiva, which could see the Supreme in samadhi but fails in its vanity; the commentator opposes the Charvakas and Saugatas.
shots.B12C363S217H02: The rope and snake image shows how the Supreme and Jiva are taken as one when true knowledge comes.
shots.B12C363S217H03: Here the usual doctrine of Jiva's deathlessness is set aside, since its merging with the Supreme may count as its death.
shots.B12C363S217H04: Pasya and apasya mean the knower and the known, and one who sees no difference is Kevala, though outwardly still a Jiva.
shots.B12C363S217H05: All men may utter Brahma or the Vedas, a liberal sentiment that fits Yajnavalkya's teaching of liberation.
shots.B12C363S218H01: The doctrine is that liberation needs acts to be destroyed first.
shots.B12C363S218H02: These are not obstacles from outer nature, so ordinary personal effort cannot remove them.
shots.B12C363S218H03: Sanchodayishyanti means questioning the king inwardly by yoga power.
shots.B12C363S218H04: Utsmayan means priding oneself on invincibility, and visesayan means overpowering.
shots.B12C363S219H01: Vaiseshikam is hard to pin down; the Vaisheshika school of Kanada resembles atomic theory and shares points with Sankhya.
shots.B12C363S219H02: Vidhi means karmakanda, and the value of acts on the path to liberation is to purify the Soul.
shots.B12C363S219H04: Holding a sceptre is one mode of life, like the triple-stick, and king and sannyasin can both gain knowledge whatever their emblems.
shots.B12C363S219H05: Janaka says that neither his royalty nor the other man's mendicancy can aid or hinder liberation, which comes through knowledge.
shots.B12C363S220H01: Changing a royal life for a mendicant's staff gains nothing.
shots.B12C363S220H02: Yukte means the Yogin; the Bombay reading is mistaken, and the Bengal vimuktasya is adopted.
shots.B12C363S220H03: The king says he made no assignation with the lady, and sannikarsha means sanketa, though both translators render it wrongly.
shots.B12C363S220H04: The faults and merits are set out in the verses that follow.
shots.B12C363S220H05: Saukshmyam means ambiguity, and Parasara's verse serves as an example of words each having several senses.
shots.B12C363S221H01: Weighing probabilities, one first takes Parasara's verse as allowing second husbands.
shots.B12C363S221H02: The tentative meaning is rejected for niyoga, since other texts conflict with it.
shots.B12C363S221H03: Prayojanam is the conduct one follows to gratify a wish, which matches the Gautama-sutra definition.
shots.B12C363S221H04: The five marks of a complete and intelligible statement are named in Nyaya and Mimamsa terms.
shots.B12C363S221H05: The commentator says the sixteen characteristics include the twenty-four Bhojadeva named in his rhetoric.
shots.B12C363S222H01: Parartham means excellent sense, not paraprayojanam.
shots.B12C363S222H02: Sulabha says the same elements and the same Chit pervade every body, so Janaka's questions are misplaced.
shots.B12C363S222H03: Creatures are said to have more or less sattwa, so sattwa seems to exist in their constitutions.
shots.B12C363S222H04: Kala means the sixteen principles beginning with prana, and desire is what makes rebirth possible.
shots.B12C363S222H05: Vidhi is righteousness and its reverse, sukra is what helps the seed grow, and vala is the effort made for desire.
shots.B12C363S223H01: The Hindu sages knew that the body's particles change constantly, and Harvey's discovery of blood circulation was also known to the Rishis.
shots.B12C363S223H02: The lamp flame looks steady but is made of successive burning of oil particles, and K.P. Singha renders both verses inaccurately.
shots.B12C363S223H03: Janaka's questions about who the lady was and whose she was are futile.
shots.B12C363S223H04: Duty, wealth and pleasure combine in seven ways, from each alone to all three together.
shots.B12C363S223H05: A king may order men, who return to report, and he must grant them interviews.
shots.B12C363S224H01: The three others are growth, decline and stability, all arising from policy, and the treasury supports the ministers as they support it.
shots.B12C363S224H02: When every kingdom has a king, no one should be proud of being a king.
shots.B12C363S224H03: Janaka rules without attachment, so he cannot claim the merit that belongs to kings.
shots.B12C363S224H04: Upaya is the posture of yoga, upanishad is hearing and reflection, upasanga is the practices of meditation, and nischaya is the conclusion about Brahma.
shots.B12C363S225H01: The na in the second line goes with vyayachcchate.
shots.B12C363S225H02: Sulabha's words are unanswerable, and Emancipation requires renouncing the household life.
shots.B12C363S225H04: The world is a place of action whose consequences are used up by enjoyment or suffering, and Nivritti stops further acts.
shots.B12C363S225H05: Kulapatam is taken as a great river town, and both translators misread kulaparam and venumivoddhatam.
shots.B12C363S226H01: One upholds righteousness by doing the duties of a Brahmana.
shots.B12C363S226H02: Prachalita-dharma means those who have fallen from righteousness, and karanabhih means acts.
shots.B12C363S226H03: The commentator says kings can gain felicity in the next world, which is not attainable even in thousands of births for others.
shots.B12C363S226H04: Rudhirapah are blood-sucking worms, and uparatam means dead.
shots.B12C363S226H05: The ten commandments are five positive ones, purity, contentment, penance, Vedic study and meditation on God, and five negative ones, against cruelty, untruth, theft, broken vows and greed for wealth.
shots.B12C363S227H01: Chirasya goes with the phrase meaning you are always blind, and the Burdwan translator confuses it with achirena.
shots.B12C363S227H02: The Burdwan version of this verse is ridiculous.
shots.B12C363S227H03: Kevalam nidhim means one's only treasure, which may be Samadhi or Brahma, and abstaining from acts is the true way to liberation.
shots.B12C363S227H05: The sight of golden trees is an omen of death.
shots.B12C363S228H01: Yavaka is a food of ghee and flour or barley, and the verse warns that death may come before it is cooked, so one should hurry.
shots.B12C363S228H02: The soul witnesses the acts of this life in the next world, and Yogins live in the soul unaware of the body, so the body's death is the act of the witnessing soul.
shots.B12C363S228H03: The Burdwan version of this verse is wrong.
shots.B12C363S228H04: Only righteousness leads a man to the path of happiness, not instructions however often repeated.
shots.B12C363S228H05: Pramadagah means a dweller in the house of heedlessness, that is Death, and pura may mean soon or before the senses are taken.
shots.B12C363S229H01: The road with self in front and self behind is the road of self-knowledge.
shots.B12C363S229H02: The last word of the second line is muchyate, not yujyate.
shots.B12C363S229H03: Srutam means knowledge from Vedic texts such as Tattwamasi, which leads to omniscience and liberation.
shots.B12C363S229H04: Relations recur over many rebirths but are not truly ours, like pieces of wood that float together and part again.
shots.B12C363S229H05: Mokshadaisikam means teaching liberation, and this section is the lesson that cleanses the heart.
shots.B12C363S230H01: Time, as a personified agent, throws creatures near or far according to their acts, holding the binding cords.
shots.B12C363S230H02: Both vernacular translators misread the first line; Bhishma says one should not speak of instances of violation.
shots.B12C363S230H03: Suka received the Vedas naturally but, by custom, formally learned them from a preceptor.
shots.B12C363S230H04: Vyasa was priest to the kings of Mithila, so his son should not claim superiority over that king.
shots.B12C363S230H05: All acts must be given up before liberation, but gradually, in the order of the modes of life.
shots.B12C363S231H01: The karanas are the inner faculties.
shots.B12C363S231H02: Liberation and omniscience reached in the first mode of life need no later stages.
shots.B12C363S231H03: One should behold the Supreme Soul by one's own soul.
shots.B12C363S231H04: Some texts read pavakam, meaning of the nature of fire, instead of papakam.
shots.B12C363S231H05: Saha is understood after manasa, so both the mind and the senses must be restrained.
shots.B12C363S232H02: The soul's gaze is turned on the soul, and the man withdraws from every worldly object.
shots.B12C363S232H03: He no longer walked like ordinary men and moved through the sky without treading the earth.
shots.B12C363S232H04: Bhimaraja is the popular name of the Lanius Malabaricus, a bird.
shots.B12C363S232H05: Penances are believed to scorch the three worlds, which is why the gods had to grant boons to Asuras and Danavas.
shots.B12C363S233H01: If the Vedas are not studied constantly, they are likely to be forgotten.
shots.B12C363S233H02: Upaplava is Rahu, and dust raised by whirlwinds in the hot season can hide the moon for hours.
shots.B12C363S233H03: The lowest order of men, who live by slaying animals, is meant.
shots.B12C363S233H04: The Bengal texts make this a triplet; the Bombay edition leaves out the third line, so the verse refers to the wind Samana or Pravaha.
shots.B12C363S233H05: Some texts read jaytamvarah, which would make the wind foremost in strength.
shots.B12C363S234H01: The Ganga is said to flow in three courses, on the earth, through the nether regions and through heaven.
shots.B12C363S234H02: The first line runs into the second.
shots.B12C363S234H03: Penances should be guarded from anger, forgiveness is a Brahmana's highest virtue, and knowledge should not be pursued for honour.
shots.B12C363S234H04: The saying about speaking what is beneficial even if it is not true is often misread; it covers cases where truth itself does harm, illustrated by a Rishi's story of travellers and robbers.
shots.B12C363S234H05: A section heading, SECTION CCCLI, marks the start of the next part.
shots.B12C363S235H01: Conquering the unconquerable means attaining Brahma.
shots.B12C363S235H02: Paravara means the Supreme Soul; the correct reading is nasyati, and the Burdwan version is meaningless.
